research:dynamics.area: Numerics of gravity, orbits, frames and time from tabletop to solar system and beyond (integrators, precision, non-inertial frames, time warp, planet-scale environment models, Newtonian limits, open ephemeris data, and a 0.5 ms A16 budget)
research:dynamics.summary:
A solar system fits the phone easily; the hard parts are precision, frames and time warp, not force count. No A16 measurement of any of this exists, so every phone figure below is scaled from desktop measurements.

Defensible budget for 0.5 ms of one A16 performance core per 60 Hz frame (ESTIMATE, assuming an A16 P-core is 1-2x the single-thread speed of the desktop CPUs measured):
- **Sun + 8 planets, Wisdom-Holman at a 5-day step:** about 300-600 steps per frame, so time warp up to about 8e9x (roughly 250-500 simulated years per wall second), with relative energy error bounded near 1e-8 and no secular drift.
- **34 bodies (Sun, planets, major moons, dwarf planets), Principia-class 12th-order at a 10-minute step:** about 16 force evaluations per frame, so warp up to about 6e5x, with errors of metres per year against its own model.
- **On-rails Kepler bodies:** at least 2,500 per frame at any warp factor, exact for two bodies.
- **Direct-sum leapfrog:** about 300-450 mutually gravitating bodies at one force evaluation per frame.
- **At 1x to 1e4x warp:** the 34-body system costs under 10 microseconds per frame amortised.

Other points the architects need:
- Float32 is unusable beyond a few km (0.5 m steps at Earth radius, 16 km at 1 AU). Float64 covers a star system (31 micrometres at 1 AU, 1 mm at 30 AU) but not a galaxy (33 km at 26,000 ly). The A16 GPU is fp32-only.
- The workshop design therefore has to live in a local, co-moving, re-based frame inside a float64 hierarchical frame tree.
- Plain leapfrog is wrong for planetary orbits: about 155,000 km of along-track error per year at 100 steps per orbit.
- Newtonian scope can be declared with numbers: Mercury 42.98 arcsec per century, 499 s light-time per AU, speeds below 0.01c.

Network limits: the fetch tool could not resolve any host, so pages were pulled with curl. arxiv.org, en.wikipedia.org and raw.githubusercontent.com were opened; JPL, NASA, Epic, the KSP wiki, readthedocs and NVIDIA were blocked, and those items are marked unverified. Pure arithmetic I ran this session is tagged DERIVED and marked verified only where its inputs are definitional or came from opened sources. I wrote helper scripts and downloads to the session scratchpad only; no project files were touched.

findings.claim: MEASURED: REBOUND WHFast integrates the Sun + 8 planets for 5 Gyr at a 5-day step in 6.82 days on one Xeon Gold 6148 core (WHFast512/AVX-512: 1.40 days; MERCURY: 46.5 days). DERIVED: 3.65e11 steps, so 1.61 microseconds per step (0.20 per planet), 0.33 for AVX-512 and 11 for MERCURY.

Principia's real-solar-system configuration integrates 34 massive bodies with a 12th-order Quinlan-Tremaine symmetric linear multistep method at a fixed 10-minute step (vessel histories: 8th order at 10 s; predictions: adaptive RKN at 1 mm and 1 mm/s tolerance). Its FAQ puts one force evaluation of all massive bodies plus one vessel at 30 microseconds (MEASURED by the authors, CPU unstated); DERIVED ceiling 600 s / 30 us = 2e7x real time on a full core, consistent with their 'very smooth at 6,000,000x with no vessels'.

ESTIMATE for 0.5 ms of one A16 P-core per frame (A16 taken as 1-2x the desktop cores above; unmeasured): 310-620 WHFast steps of Sun + 8 planets, i.e. warp of 8e9x to 1.6e10x at a 5-day step; or about 16 force evaluations of the 34-body system, i.e. warp of about 6e5x (range 3e5x to 1.2e6x) at a 10-minute step. Direct-sum leapfrog at an ESTIMATED 5-10 ns per pair gives 50,000-100,000 pair interactions, i.e. about 320-450 mutually gravitating bodies at one evaluation per frame.
findings.source: DERIVED this session from the two measured anchors above; A16-versus-desktop ratio and ns-per-pair are estimates (Geekbench figures in 01-research.md are themselves unverified)

findings.claim: Wisdom-Holman energy error is bounded and scales as O(mass-ratio x dt^2); WHFast removes the linear secular drift, leaving only a random walk from round-off (Brouwer's law). MEASURED: outer Solar System at a 1.5-day step holds about 1e-14 relative energy error with symplectic correctors and about 1e-10.5 without; Mercury needs more than 20 steps per 88-day orbit (dt about 4 days); a 5-day step kept the median relative energy error below 1e-8 over 40 Gyr.

IAS15 is a 15th-order adaptive Gauss-Radau integrator that holds machine precision (about 1e-16) over 1e9 orbits at about 100 steps per orbit and handles close encounters and velocity-dependent forces. DERIVED cost: 7 substages x about 2 predictor-corrector iterations = about 14 force evaluations per step, about 1,400 per orbit; a 10x larger step raises the error by 1e15, so it suits a reference oracle, not a real-time integrator.

Close encounters are handled by hybrid schemes: MERCURIUS and TRACE run Wisdom-Holman normally and switch to IAS15 or Bulirsch-Stoer inside a critical radius (documentation example: 4 Hill radii). MEASURED: TRACE matches MERCURIUS accuracy with a 12x speed-up for planet-planet encounters and is 15x to 41x faster than IAS15 in scattering and lunar-accretion tests.

DERIVED: plain leapfrog/Verlet on a circular orbit has relative frequency error (omega*dt)^2/24 although its energy error stays bounded. For Earth's orbit that is about 155,000 km of along-track error per year at 100 steps per orbit, 1,546 km at 1,000 steps and 5.6 m at 60-second steps. Leapfrog is second-order, symplectic, time-reversible and stable only for dt < 2/omega.
findings.source: Derivation this session from the Verlet relation 4*sin^2(theta/2) = (omega*dt)^2; order and stability limit from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leapfrog_integration (opened)

findings.claim: DERIVED position step (ULP) for float32 / float64: Earth radius 0.5 m / 0.93 nm; Moon distance 32 m / 60 nm; 1 AU 16.4 km / 31 micrometres; 30 AU 524 km / 0.98 mm; 1 light-year 1.07e9 m / 2 m; 26,000 ly 1.76e13 m (118 AU) / 32.8 km; 100,000 ly 7.0e13 m / 131 km. Velocity step: float32 is 0.49 mm/s at 7.67 km/s (LEO) and 1.95 mm/s at 29.78 km/s; float64 is 9e-13 and 3.6e-12 m/s.
findings.source: Direct IEEE-754 computation this session (python struct and math.ulp); float32 step sizes cross-checked against the table in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/godotengine/godot-docs/master/tutorials/physics/large_world_coordinates.rst (opened)

findings.claim: Godot's documentation recommends single precision only out to 4-8 km for first- and third-person 3D games (steps of 0.2-0.5 mm) and 64 km for any 3D game. Beyond that it offers an all-double build with a stated performance and memory penalty that 'may not perform well on low-end mobile devices', emulates doubles in shaders with pairs of floats, and names origin shifting as the low-end alternative.

Unreal Engine 5 Large World Coordinates moved world positions to doubles with a default world limit of 88 million km (0.59 AU); DERIVED float64 step there is 15 micrometres, so one UE5 frame does not span a solar system. KSP's API documents a FloatingOrigin class and a Krakensbane class 'used to overcome the floating point precision errors' by re-basing position and velocity around the active vessel; the specific thresholds I recall (6 km, 750 m/s) could not be confirmed.
findings.source: Search excerpts only; could not open https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/large-world-coordinates-in-unreal-engine-5 or https://www.kerbalspaceprogram.com/ksp/api/class_krakensbane.html (hosts blocked)

findings.claim: Stock KSP uses patched conics with planets on fixed rails and no n-body gravity. To replace that, Principia had to alter the stock Jool moon system (unstable under n-body: orbits enlarged, Bop made retrograde), use a different integrator (Blanes-Moan) for that system, add double-double summation, and add geopotentials (Earth to degree 10, Moon to degree and order 30). It rejected Kepler rails for planets because solving Kepler's equation costs more than the N^2 forces at about 20 bodies, and rejected multithreading for a 30-microsecond task.
findings.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerbal_Space_Program ; Principia FAQ and Change-Log wiki pages via raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/mockingbirdnest/Principia/ (all opened)

findings.claim: The IAS15 paper states that floating point destroys Galilean invariance: translating a Solar System held in AU units by 1e16 loses all relative-position information, and force accuracy can be no better than relative-position accuracy. This is the primary-source argument for storing each body relative to its parent (hierarchical frames) and never in one global frame.

DERIVED integer ranges: int64 at 1 mm resolution spans +/-9.22e15 m (61,650 AU, 0.975 ly), enough for a star system out to the Oort cloud; int64 at 1 micrometre spans only +/-61.6 AU; int128 at 1 micrometre spans +/-1.8e16 ly. A galaxy therefore needs either 128-bit positions or a two-level address (star-system index plus an int64 or float64 offset).
findings.source: Integer-range arithmetic computed this session (definitional inputs)

findings.claim: Surface gravity derived, not asserted: GM/R^2 = 9.820 m/s^2 at Earth's mean radius; centrifugal omega^2*R = 0.0339 m/s^2 at the equator (DERIVED); MEASURED sea-level g is 9.780 at the equator and 9.832 at the poles. The MEASURED vertical gradient is 0.3086 mGal/m (3.086e-6 per s^2), so uniform g across a 10 m workshop is wrong by about 3 ppm, while Coriolis 2*omega*v = 1.46e-3 m/s^2 at 10 m/s (1.5e-4 g) is the largest term neglected at workshop scale.

DERIVED tidal gradient at 400 km altitude: n^2 = 1.28e-6 per s^2; in the orbiting frame a vehicle is stretched radially by 3n^2 = 3.85e-6 m/s^2 per metre (0.39 micro-g per metre) and compressed by n^2 across the orbit plane. Gravity-gradient torque is 3n^2 * r x (I r), at most 1.5 n^2 * (Imax - Imin): 0.016 N*m for a 1-tonne, 10 m rod, with a libration period of orbit period / sqrt(3) = 53 min.
findings.source: memory (standard astrodynamics formulas); numbers computed this session from GM = 3.986e14 m^3/s^2

findings.claim: Earth's J2 is 1.0826e-3 and drives node regression of -1.5*J2*(R/p)^2*n*cos(i): -3.68 degrees/day for an 800 km, 56-degree orbit (source example). DERIVED: -5.0 degrees/day for the ISS, about 590 km/day of cross-track error if J2 is omitted; the perturbing acceleration is about 1.5*J2*g = 0.016 m/s^2 at the surface. Principia found Mars's C22/S22 terms necessary for Phobos.

A two-body orbit can be advanced exactly over any time span by a universal-variable Kepler solve (one equation covering elliptic, parabolic and hyperbolic cases via Stumpff functions). WHFast512 uses a fixed 2 Halley + 2 Newton iterations with truncated series to reach 1e-13 relative error, with no library trig calls. DERIVED: at most 0.2 microseconds per body, so at least 2,500 on-rails bodies per 0.5 ms regardless of warp factor.
findings.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_variable_formulation ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.05683 Appendix A (opened); per-body bound derived from the measured 1.61 us step for 8 planets

findings.claim: Time-warp precedent: stock KSP's maximum warp is 100,000x. Principia keeps full n-body integration under warp and reports it smooth at 100,000x with 20 vessels, 'janky but usable' at 1,000,000x and smooth at 6,000,000x with no vessels (desktop); its eclipse predictions lose 'a few minutes of accuracy after a century or so'.
findings.source: Principia FAQ and Change-Log wiki pages via raw.githubusercontent.com (opened)

findings.claim: State that can be advanced analytically without breaking conservation: two-body orbits; torque-free rigid rotation (closed form in Jacobi elliptic functions, conserving angular momentum and kinetic energy); lumped thermal relaxation (exponential for linear exchange, closed form for pure radiation); constant-load battery discharge. KSP freezes vessels under on-rails warp into Kepler points with no forces, torques or part physics. Contact, atmospheric flight and close encounters cannot be put on rails.
findings.source: memory (KSP on-rails behaviour and the closed-form solutions); conservation properties of torque-free rotation checked at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poinsot%27s_ellipsoid

findings.claim: Hierarchical (block) timesteps place bodies on power-of-two rungs dt_n = dt_0/2^n and let them change rung only at synchronisation points. Variable steps break the symplectic property of leapfrog, but time-symmetric variants recover good long-term energy behaviour; the 4th-order Hermite scheme is the standard for collisional n-body work.
findings.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.1082 (Dehnen & Read review, PDF opened, section 2.3)

findings.claim: Barnes-Hut trees give O(N log N) but do not pay at solar-system counts: for N = 100 at opening angle 1 the tree needs 902 cell-particle plus 306 particle-particle interactions against 4,950 direct pairs, about 4x fewer at reduced accuracy. Few-body steps cost microseconds, so the WHFast512 authors and Principia both conclude that parallelising them across threads is counter-productive.

No published n-body throughput for any mobile or integrated GPU was found. The only anchor is GPU Gems 3: about 1e10 pair interactions per second on a GeForce 8800 GTX at N = 16,384 (38 steps/s). ESTIMATE for the fp32-only A16 GPU from its 1.7 TFLOPS theoretical figure: 5e9 to 1.2e10 interactions/s sustained, i.e. about 2,000-3,500 all-pairs bodies per 1 ms, usable only in a local frame because float32 has 16 km steps at 1 AU.
findings.source: Search excerpt of https://developer.nvidia.com/gpugems/GPUGems3/gpugems3_ch31.html (host blocked); A16 GPU figures from 01-research.md (unverified there)

findings.claim: Hydrostatic atmosphere: the barometric formula's scale height R*T/(M*g) is about 8.4 km in the troposphere (DERIVED 8.43 km at 288.15 K). The U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 starts at 101,325 Pa and 288.15 K with a -6.5 K/km lapse rate and is tabulated in 7 layers to 86 km; measured density falls by a factor of 9,600 by 70 km (mean scale height 7.64 km).

Re-entry heating correlation: Sutton-Graves stagnation heat flux q = k*sqrt(rho/Rn)*v^3 with k = 1.7415e-4 kg^0.5/m for Earth air. On the Hayabusa2 capsule it gave a 9.0 MW/m^2 peak, 15-18% below the Detra-Kemp-Riddell correlation, so it is an empirical law good to roughly +/-20%. DERIVED example: 7.8 km/s, rho 3.1e-4 kg/m^3, 1 m nose radius gives 1.46 MW/m^2 and a 2,340 K radiative-equilibrium wall at emissivity 0.85.

Stellar flux: the solar constant is MEASURED at 1.361 kW/m^2 at 1 AU (0.1% higher at solar maximum). DERIVED by inverse square: 9,088 W/m^2 at Mercury, 586 at Mars, 50.3 at Jupiter, 1.51 at Neptune. DERIVED radiative-equilibrium temperature of Earth at Bond albedo 0.3 is 254-255 K, about 33 K below the observed mean surface temperature (288 K, from memory), which is the error of a no-greenhouse model.

Tides and limits: lunar tidal acceleration at Earth's surface is 1.1e-7 g and solar 0.52e-7 g. The fluid Roche limit is 2.44*R*(rho_primary/rho_satellite)^(1/3) (rigid-body coefficient 1.26, from memory); DERIVED for Earth-Moon: 18,370 km fluid, 9,480 km rigid. Sphere of influence is a*(m/M)^(2/5): 0.929 million km for Earth.

What Newton gets wrong: general relativity adds 42.980 arcsec/century to Mercury's perihelion out of 574.10 observed (DERIVED: 23 km per orbit, about 9,600 km per century at perihelion). GPS clocks gain 38.6 microseconds/day (DERIVED 11.6 km/day of range). DERIVED light-time is 499.0 s per AU (Earth moves 14,860 km meanwhile) and 4.16 h at 30 AU; gamma-1 is 3.3e-10 in LEO, 4.9e-9 at Earth's orbital speed, 5e-5 at 0.01c and 0.5% at 0.1c.

The Solar System is chaotic with a Lyapunov time of 2-230 million years depending on the study. A 15 m error in Earth's position makes its position unpredictable over about 100 Myr (Laskar), and a 0.38 mm error in Mercury's position makes its eccentricity unpredictable after about 200 Myr (Brown & Rein). At the highest warp factors only bit-exact replay, not positional accuracy, can be guaranteed.

Open data: JPL DE440 is 114 MB (years 1550-2650), de440s 32 MB (1849-2150), de421 17 MB (1900-2050) and DE441 3.1 GB (-13200 to 17191), stored as Chebyshev coefficients in 32-day segments, with inner-planet orbits known to sub-kilometre accuracy. VSOP87 analytic series are good to 1 arcsec (DERIVED 725 km at 1 AU) over 4,000 years. Principia seeds from JPL Horizons state vectors (1950-01-01) and integrates itself. NASA policy: material is 'not protected by copyright unless noted'; JPL/Caltech-specific terms and the NASA fact sheets could not be opened.

implications: Add a celestial tier above the mechanism tier: CPU, float64, single-threaded, with every body stored relative to its parent in a frame tree (galaxy, star system, planet, moon, local workshop). The existing workshop design becomes the leaf frame and never sees absolute coordinates.

The mechanism and matter tiers must run in a local frame that is re-based in both position and velocity (floating origin plus velocity re-basing). Float32 is acceptable only within about 4-8 km of the local origin; the fp32-only GPU can receive gravity only as a uniform vector plus an optional 3x3 tidal-gradient matrix computed on the CPU in float64.

Uniform g stops being a constant and becomes a derived, declared approximation: g_eff = GM/R^2 minus the centrifugal term, with Coriolis, Euler and tidal terms reported as neglected or enabled. Their sizes are known (Coriolis 1.5e-4 g at 10 m/s, gradient 3 ppm per 10 m, lunar tide 1.1e-7 g), so the Reality Report can list them, and fictitious-force work needs its own ledger account distinct from numerical loss.

Give each gravitating body one of three declared propagation modes: on-rails Kepler (exact two-body, cost independent of warp), symplectic n-body (Wisdom-Holman or a high-order multistep; bounded energy error, cost linear in warp), and a high-order adaptive reference (IAS15 class) used for close encounters and as the test oracle.

Do not use plain leapfrog for planetary or moon orbits: its along-track error is about 155,000 km per year at 100 steps per orbit. Use Kepler-splitting or rails there and keep leapfrog-type stepping for the local 480 Hz physics.

Time warp should be a ladder with a declared fidelity at each rung: full physics at low warp; mechanisms frozen into rigid composites with point-mass orbit and analytic attitude at medium warp; 34-body n-body up to about 6e5x; planets-only Wisdom-Holman up to about 8e9x; pure rails beyond. The gravity budget is 3% of one core, so the thermal governor is unaffected.

Bit-exact replay extends to the celestial tier only if the Kepler solver avoids library sin/cos/pow and uses fixed iteration counts with its own series (as WHFast512 does), and fused multiply-add contraction is pinned identically on phone, browser and build server.

Tree codes, GPU n-body and multithreading are unnecessary for a solar system (up to about 400 direct-sum bodies fit the budget). Rings, asteroid belts and debris should be massless on-rails particles, optionally evaluated on the GPU from orbital elements relative to their parent.

Planet-scale environment should be analytic fields evaluated on demand, each registered as a declared model with a stated error: layered hydrostatic atmosphere, inverse-square stellar flux, radiative equilibrium (no greenhouse: -33 K for Earth), Sutton-Graves heating (about +/-20%), J2-only gravity (omitting it costs about 590 km/day cross-track in low Earth orbit).

The charter's out-of-scope list can gain numeric entries: relativity (Mercury 43 arcsec/century; valid for speeds below 0.01c and GM/(r c^2) below 1e-8), finite light-time (499 s per AU), and long-term predictability beyond about 10 Myr.

Ship only initial state vectors and GM values for about 34 bodies (a few kB) and integrate on device; keep the 32 MB de440s file off the device as a CI oracle for tests such as position error against DE440 after 1, 10 and 100 years.

'Or even more' means more hierarchy levels, not a bigger solver: int64 millimetres covers one star system to 0.97 ly, a galaxy needs a star index plus offset or 128-bit positions, stars stay on rails, and only one star system needs to be awake for n-body at a time (the same sleeping idea the plan already uses).
open_questions: What do a Wisdom-Holman step, a pair interaction and a Kepler solve actually cost in float64 on an A16 P-core, natively and in Safari WebAssembly (including 2-wide f64 SIMD)? Every phone figure here is scaled from Xeon and unspecified desktop measurements; the Phase 0a probe should add these three micro-benchmarks.
Does a float64 Kepler solver and n-body step replay bit-exactly across Safari WebAssembly, native arm64 and the x86 build server once fused multiply-add and transcendental functions are controlled?

How large are the energy and momentum ledger discontinuities at hand-offs (rails to n-body, n-body to local rigid-body frame, sphere-of-influence or frame-tree boundaries, inertial to rotating surface frame at 465 m/s), and what tolerance is acceptable?

What are the rules for freezing a live mechanism or matter region into a rigid composite for warp and thawing it again without violating the ledger (stored elastic energy, sloshing liquid, spinning parts, hot parts)?

Which step size and integrator keep the chosen body set (including fast moons such as Phobos at 7.65 h and Io at 1.77 days) within a stated error against DE440 over 1-100 years, and is that body set stable over game timescales under our integrator?

Should Coriolis and tidal-gradient terms be on by default in the workshop frame? The solver cost is negligible, but it needs validation tests (Foucault pendulum, free-fall deflection, gravity-gradient libration at 53 min).

How should vessels be integrated at high warp within budget: fixed 10 s steps cost about 167 steps per vessel per frame at 1e5x, so an adaptive or Kepler-plus-perturbation (Encke-type) scheme needs prototyping and an accuracy test.

Can correlation-level entry heating and drag be coupled to the mechanism and matter tiers in a way that passes a published case (for example the Hayabusa2 capsule's 9-12 MW/m^2 peak), given that the matter tier cannot resolve hypersonic flow?
If debris or ring swarms are wanted, what all-pairs or on-rails particle throughput does the A16 GPU actually sustain? No published mobile figure exists.

research:worlds.area: Multi-scale representation, level of detail, persistence and precedent: how an engine that can afford litres of detailed matter can contain a planet, solar system or galaxy
research:worlds.summary:
Every shipped precedent and the numerical literature point to the same architecture: a tree of reference frames (galaxy integer grid or fixed point, star-system f64, body-fixed f64, small f32 region co-moving with the player), closed-form or pre-integrated motion for everything unobserved, a deterministic generator plus a journal of deltas for content, and conservative hand-offs between levels. The existing workshop design becomes the innermost region; what must be added is an orbital/aggregate tier, a frame tree, a generator-plus-journal world store and a hand-off contract that restricts to the same conserved quantities at every level. The documented failures in shipped games are almost all at hand-offs (orbit shifts when entering time warp, docking that does not conserve momentum, mined mass restored on reload, terrain edits silently reverting), which is exactly where a first-principles engine has to be stricter than its precedents.

Evidence quality: en.wikipedia.org, arxiv.org and www.gdcvault.com were NOT reachable from this session (DNS failure), nor were developer blogs, university or journalism sites. Only raw.githubusercontent.com fetches succeeded, so verified=true items are source code and documentation hosted on GitHub (KSP API docs, KSPCommunityFixes, Principia, Space Engineers source, Luanti, godot_voxel, AMReX, Orbiter, REBOUND, Jolt, Godot, big_space, Celestia, BurnMan PREM table, MDN). All statements about Outer Wilds, Star Citizen, KSP2, Noita, Universe Sandbox, Elite, No Man's Sky, SpaceEngine, Dual Universe, Children of a Dead Earth, Carlson-Hodgins and Chenney rest on search-result excerpts and are marked verified=false. No measurement exists for generation or streaming cost on an iPhone 15; those are open questions.

Out of reach on a phone (declare, do not fake): particle-resolution matter beyond the awake region (Earth is 3.6e22 times the 30 L budget, DERIVED); global oceans, atmospheres, weather and climate as fluid dynamics; planetary collisions and hypervelocity impacts (closing speeds above material sound speed break the rigid/incompressible assumptions); continuous simulation of unobserved regions; exact retroactive evaluation of chaotic unobserved matter (piles, splashes); mutual N-body dynamics of a galaxy or feedback of vessels on planets; time warp with workshop-tier matter awake; two full-budget detail regions at once under about 4 W; storing rather than generating a galaxy (4e11 systems at 1 byte each is 400 GB, DERIVED); relativity and light-time; first-principles formation of star systems at run time.

findings.claim: DERIVED (IEEE-754 spacing 2^(floor(log2 x)-23) for f32, -52 for f64; computed this session): f32 resolves 6.25 cm at 600 km, 0.5 m at Earth's radius and 16.4 km at 1 AU; f64 resolves 0.93 nm at Earth's radius, 30 micrometres at 1 AU, about 1 mm at 30 AU, 2 m at 1 light-year and 65 km at 5e20 m. MEASURED (Godot docs table): f32 step is about 0.03 mm at 256-512 m, 0.5 mm at 4-8 km, 3.9 mm at 32-65 km.

MEASURED (docs): the Rust crate big_space uses nestable integer grids (i8 to i128) with an f32 transform relative to each cell centre, giving 0.5 mm worst-case precision; an i64 grid spans 19.5 million light-years, children of a grid inherit a planet's motion in high precision, and it claims 'absolute coordinates without drift, unlike camera-relative or periodic recentering'. Celestia's UniversalCoord is a fixed-point (R128) type for 'millimeters to thousands of light years'.

MEASURED (KSP API docs): vessels are loaded only within about 2.5 km of the active vessel and are packed/unpacked at about 300 m; 'CelestialBodies and on-rails Vessels follow their Orbits exactly'; a vessel goes on rails when it exits loading distance or enters time warp; the Krakensbane velocity frame engages at about 750 m/s; on-rails warp rates were 1 to 100,000x (v0.18.2).

MEASURED (community bug-fix list for KSP 1.12): shipped hand-off defects include the active vessel's orbit 'moving randomly when engaging timewarp' under CPU load, docking ports that did not conserve momentum (fix: average the acquire force between the two ports), asteroid mass 'restored to 100% when reloading after having mined it down to 0%', and unrecoverable part position drift on robotics and docking ports.

MEASURED (Principia docs): stock KSP keeps a vessel 'within the sphere of influence of a single celestial' (two-body conics); under true N-body gravity the stock Jool moon system is unstable and Principia makes Bop retrograde to fix it. Principia integrates the solar system ahead of time, lets only celestials exert gravity (vessels are test particles), and reports time warp smooth at 100,000x and at 6,000,000x with no vessels, with slowdown caused by vessel count and trajectory prediction.

MEASURED (Space Engineers source): physics is split into clusters with IdealClusterSize 20,000 m, a 2,000 m minimum distance from the border and a split threshold of 40,000 m; a cluster is created around each non-static object, overlapping clusters are unioned and re-split along the longest axis, and an object's offset is its cluster's AABB centre. DERIVED from the Godot table: a 10 km half-size gives about 1 mm worst-case f32 resolution.

MEASURED (source and docs): Space Engineers stores voxels in an octree whose leaves are either read-only procedural 'provider' leaves (only the cell key is saved) or 16x16x16-voxel micro-octree leaves materialised on first write; the save holds the serialized generator plus edited leaves. godot_voxel states 'By default, only modified blocks are saved'.

MEASURED (Luanti docs): the world is stored as 16x16x16-node map blocks (u16+u8+u8 per node, so 16,384 bytes raw per block, DERIVED) compressed whole with zstd and stamped with a u32 last-saved time; only blocks near players are active, and unattended areas are caught up lazily: ABM catch_up (default true) raises the trigger chance on return, LBMs receive dtime_s (seconds since the block was last active) and node timers receive total elapsed time.

MEASURED (AMReX docs): at a coarse-fine interface 'the area-weighted fluxes from the fine grid advance do not in general match the underlying flux from the coarse grid face', so conservation is restored by a reflux correction applied to the adjacent coarse cells; fine levels are subcycled ('advanced r times using a coarse grid time step reduced by a factor of r'), and covered coarse cells are overwritten with the average of the fine cells.

DERIVED (Koenig's theorem): replacing N bodies by one rigid aggregate with the same mass, linear momentum, angular momentum and inertia tensor always removes the kinetic energy of internal relative motion, dE = sum of 0.5*m_i*|v_i - v_cm - w x r_i|^2 >= 0. A conservative demotion must therefore book dE into an internal-energy account, and promotion cannot recover the micro-state unless a seed or record is stored.
findings.source: own derivation from classical mechanics (no external source opened)

findings.claim: DERIVED (GM_Earth 3.986e14 m^3/s^2, r = 6,771 km): a 400 km orbit has v = 7.67 km/s, n = 1.133e-3 rad/s and a 92.4 min period; in the co-orbiting frame tidal acceleration is 3n^2x = 5.8e-5 m/s^2 at 15 m and Coriolis is 2.3e-3 m/s^2 per m/s. An f32 velocity near 7.7 km/s has a 4.9e-4 m/s step, 2.4% of the 0.0204 m/s that 1 g adds per 480 Hz substep, versus 6.1e-5 m/s below 1 km/s.
findings.source: own derivation computed this session (constants from memory); consistent with KSP's 750 m/s Krakensbane threshold in the KSP API docs

findings.claim: DERIVED: an Earth-to-Mars Hohmann transfer takes 259 days (half the period of an a = 1.262 AU ellipse), which is 224 s at KSP's 100,000x warp; a fixed 480 Hz solver cannot be warped, so all awake matter must be demotable to closed-form state first. At 10 km/s closing speed bodies move 20.8 m per 480 Hz substep and 167 m per 60 Hz frame.

MEASURED (Orbiter source defaults): the open-source Orbiter simulator enables Encke orbit stabilisation by default (perturbation limit 0.05, step limit 0.01) and selects the integrator by step size, RK2/RK4/RK6/RK8 at time-step targets of 0.1, 2, 20 and 200-500 s; nonspherical gravity and gravity-gradient torque exist but default to off.

MEASURED (README): the research N-body code REBOUND ships symplectic integrators (WHFast, LEAPFROG, SABA), a 'high accuracy non-symplectic integrator with adaptive time-stepping' (IAS15), hybrid integrators that switch method for close encounters (MERCURIUS, TRACE) and a Simulationarchive 'for exact reproducibility of N-body simulations'.

MEASURED (PREM table shipped with BurnMan): Earth's whole radial structure is 94 rows; density is 13,088 kg/m^3 and pressure 363.85 GPa at the centre, density jumps from 5,566 to 9,903 kg/m^3 at the core-mantle boundary (r = 3,480 km) and is 2,600 kg/m^3 at the surface. DERIVED: a uniform-density Earth gives P_c = 3GM^2/(8*pi*R^4) = 172 GPa, 2.1 times too low, so a layered compressible model is required.

MEASURED (MDN): WebKit lets one origin store 'up to around 60% of total disk' in browser apps and Home Screen web apps (80% across origins); Safari deletes script-written data after seven days of browser use without interaction; writes beyond quota fail with QuotaExceededError; OPFS falls under the same quota, offers in-place writes, and its synchronous handles work only in Web Workers. DERIVED: 60% of a 128 GB phone (capacity from memory) is 76.8 GB at most, in practice bounded by free space.

MEASURED (docs): Jolt Physics says f32 is 'accurate enough' if 'all simulation takes place within roughly 5 km from the origin', its double-precision mode runs '5-10% slower' and cross-platform determinism costs about 8%; Godot recommends f32 limits of 4,096 m (first person) to 8,192 m (third person) and warns double precision 'may perform poorly on low-end mobile devices' while shaders stay single precision.

DERIVED: Earth's volume is 1.08e24 L, 3.6e22 times a 30 L detailed budget; its surface at 5 cm cells is 2.0e17 cells for one layer; a galaxy of 4e11 systems at 1 byte each is 400 GB, more than the phone's total storage. An i64 tick counter at 480 Hz spans 6.1e8 years, while f64 seconds degrade to 0.48 microseconds at 100 years and 4 s at 1e9 years.

DERIVED: surface gravity then scales as M^0.44 for rocky planets.

DERIVED (textbook formulas, constants from memory): from mass, radius, temperature, composition and orbit alone, Earth's atmospheric scale height H = kT/(mu*m_u*g) comes out at 8.4 km, its equilibrium temperature T_sun*sqrt(R_sun/2a)*(1-A)^0.25 at 254 K, its sphere of influence at 925,000 km and its Hill radius at 1.50e6 km.

findings.claim: Search excerpts only: Elite Dangerous models about 400 billion systems, generated by 'Stellar Forge' in the client from a seeded generator so the same coordinates give the same result, with real catalogue stars (Hipparcos, Gliese) where data exist; Frontier says each system 'is formed from first principles' but no reachable source documents the physics. The open StarGen lineage (Dole, Fogg 1985, Burdick 1988) is likewise seeded and reproducible.

Search excerpts only: Star Citizen moved physics and positioning to 64-bit world coordinates while rendering stays 32-bit, and its zone system gives each ship interior its own physics grid so the ship moves as one master item ('You just update the master, not the children').

Search excerpts only: KSP2's physics engineer wrote that on Kerbin (600,000 m radius) f32 positions are accurate to about 10 cm (DERIVED here: 6.25 cm), so KSP2 combined a floating origin with hierarchical positioning (a tree of offsets relative to nearby objects) and targeted collisions at 10 km/s or more; the creative director said applying N-body physics made the system 'fire moons at planets'.

Search excerpts only: Outer Wilds runs its whole solar system as a continuous Unity physics simulation ('things are changing and happening whether you're there or not') but at miniature scale, with planets tens of kilometres apart and orbiting 'way faster because everything is smaller-scale'; community sources (not developers) say it keeps the player at the origin.

Search excerpts only: Noita divides its simulated world into 64x64-cell chunks, each with a dirty rectangle so only changed cells update, and (secondary source) streams 512x512 world chunks, saving old ones to disk and keeping about 12 alive.
findings.source: https://80.lv/articles/noita-a-game-based-on-falling-sand-simulation/ and GDC 2019 talk https://gdcvault.com/play/1025695/Exploring-the-Tech-and-Design (not reachable; search excerpts)

findings.claim: Search excerpts only: Universe Sandbox integrates gravity as an N-body problem in small steps and automatically limits how fast simulated time may run 'while still maintaining relatively accurate orbits'; its planet surfaces are coarse 'Surface Grids' in which water volume moves cell to cell each step.
findings.source: https://universesandbox.com/faq and https://universesandbox.com/blog/?p=1704 (not reachable; search excerpts)

findings.claim: Search excerpts only (player reports, not Hello Games): No Man's Sky caps stored terrain edits per save at roughly 20,000-30,000, and beyond the cap the oldest edits revert so dug terrain reappears.

Search excerpts only: Carlson and Hodgins (Graphics Interface 1997, pp. 1-8) simulated less important creatures with cheaper models (fewer degrees of freedom, hybrid kinematic/dynamic, or purely kinematic) and switched between levels, with the acceptance test that the outcome of the game is essentially unchanged and the viewer's perception of motion is the same.

Search excerpts only: Chenney and Forsyth (SI3D 1997, pp. 55-58) named the consistency problem of simulation culling (what state a culled system should be in when the view returns); re-simulating the whole unseen interval causes lag, so later work (Chenney, Arikan, Forsyth, Eurographics 2001) replaces out-of-view dynamics with cheaper discrete-event proxy models.

Search excerpts only, weak: Space Engineers' 2014 'super-large worlds' update is reported to have raised the safe world radius from about 10 km (f32 Havok) to about 1e9 km using cluster-relative coordinates; SpaceEngine ships over 130,000 catalogued real objects and generates the rest; Dual Universe advertises 25 cm voxels on procedurally generated planets; Children of a Dead Earth advertises an N-body simulator at 1:1 solar-system scale.

implications: Frame tree instead of one world space: galaxy level as integer grid or fixed point; each star system in barycentric f64 metres (about 1 mm resolution out to 30 AU, DERIVED); each body in a body-fixed f64 frame; each awake region in a local f32 frame. A single f64 frame must not span more than one star system (2 m resolution at 1 light-year, DERIVED). No absolute position is ever stored in f32.

Keep an awake region small: within about 500 m of its origin f32 resolves about 0.03 mm (MEASURED, Godot table), which suits a 480 Hz mechanism solver; treat a few kilometres as the hard cap (Jolt's 5 km guidance, Space Engineers' 10 km cluster half-size gives about 1 mm).

The region frame is itself a physical object with f64 position and velocity (and rotation on a planet surface). The solvers see only velocities relative to it (KSP re-bases velocity at about 750 m/s), and the frame's tidal, Coriolis and centrifugal terms are applied as explicit body forces and entered in the ledger. This is how a vehicle interior or a region at orbital speed stays inside the existing workshop tiers.

Add an orbital/aggregate tier beneath the mechanism tier: a whole vehicle or settled body is one record (mass by material, centre of mass, momentum, angular momentum, inertia tensor, internal energy, inventory) propagated in closed form or with a symplectic/high-order integrator. Massive bodies follow a deterministic ephemeris computed as a function of time (analytic or integrated ahead of time, as Principia does); vessels are test particles under summed gravity. Both are declared approximations on the fidelity ladder.

Prefer summed gravity from an ephemeris over patched-conic sphere-of-influence switching: it removes a discontinuous hand-off, costs little (ESTIMATE: 30 bodies x 1,000 vessels x 60 Hz = 1.8 million force evaluations per second) and supports time warp because ephemeris state is a pure function of time.

One hand-off contract for every level: each representation must restrict to the same conserved record (mass per material, linear and angular momentum, kinetic and internal energy, volume), and promotion must satisfy restrict(promote(c)) == c bit-exactly on the CPU. Kinetic energy lost when coarsening is booked to internal energy in a new ledger account (it is always >= 0, DERIVED), never dropped.

Hand off only at quiescent states (asleep, in equilibrium, no contact with still-awake matter) and use hysteresis between promote and demote radii, as KSP does with separate load/unload and pack/unpack distances. Where a boundary must cut live matter, treat it like an AMR coarse-fine interface and account for the flux mismatch explicitly.

World = versioned deterministic generator (CPU, bit-exact, seeded) + journal of deltas. Store only what the player changed (edited voxel leaves, moved bodies, inventories); compact old deltas into coarser conservative summaries instead of evicting them. Silent reversion (No Man's Sky reports) or reset on reload (KSP asteroid mass bug) would break the mass ledger and must be impossible by construction; on quota exhaustion, refuse or coarsen and report it.

No background simulation of unobserved regions. Classify every process as (a) closed form in elapsed time (orbits, conduction toward equilibrium, battery self-discharge), evaluated lazily from a stored tick as Luanti does with dtime_s; (b) relaxing to an equilibrium that needs no history (liquid to hydrostatic level), jumped to with the dissipated energy booked as heat; or (c) chaotic and history-dependent, frozen and declared as such.

Time warp is legal only when no workshop-tier matter is awake; requesting warp demotes everything through the conservative hand-off first, and the warp factor is part of the replay log. Use integer ticks (i64 at 480 Hz spans 6.1e8 years, DERIVED) rather than f64 seconds as the master clock.

The thermal budget is global, not per region: two vehicles far apart share the same roughly 4 W envelope from the existing plan, so the governor's 'amount of awake matter' becomes an allocation across regions, with non-controlled regions pushed to the aggregate tier first.

Planets are data derived from laws: a radial table from integrating hydrostatic equilibrium with material equations of state (Earth's reference model is 94 rows, well under 10 kB), giving g(r), P(r), density and moment of inertia; terrain and regolith as layered columns of database materials sampled deterministically on demand; atmosphere from scale height. Each generated parameter is labelled catalogue (measured), derived from law, or sampled from a distribution (artistic or statistical).

Region merge and docking: before contact, move both regions into one frame at their common centre of mass (Space Engineers unions overlapping clusters and re-splits), and test momentum conservation across docking in CI because the reference game shipped without it. Swept collision tests are needed whenever relative motion exceeds a cell per substep (20.8 m per substep at 10 km/s, DERIVED); impacts faster than the material sound speed need a separate declared coarse model.

Storage design for iOS: append-only journal in OPFS through a synchronous access handle in a worker, navigator.storage.persist() requested, tab-kill-safe, with periodic compaction; assume Safari may evict after seven days without interaction when not installed to the Home Screen, and treat QuotaExceededError as a normal, reported state.

The lesson from Outer Wilds versus KSP: simulating a whole system continuously works only at miniature scale; at real scale every precedent uses rails plus a small physics region plus time warp. The engine should say which of the two a game has chosen rather than promise both.
open_questions: What does deterministic generation cost on an iPhone 15 in single-threaded WebAssembly (for example one 32^3 block of layered terrain materials from a seed), and therefore how fast can the awake region move over a surface inside a 1-2 ms per-frame budget? No measurement was found; any figure today is an ESTIMATE.

How large are the conservation errors and visible pops on a demote-then-promote round trip of a pile, a liquid volume and a jointed machine, and how much kinetic energy lands in the 'unresolved to internal' account each time?

Does a Home Screen web app on iOS 26 actually get multi-gigabyte OPFS writes and a granted persist(), and what is the sustained write throughput of a synchronous access handle in a worker? The 60% figure is a documented ceiling, not a measurement on this phone.
How fast does the delta journal grow in real play (bytes per minute of digging, building and moving objects), and what compaction ratio do conservative summaries achieve?

Can the mechanism tier at 480 Hz in f32 resolve the fictitious forces of its own frame (Earth-surface Coriolis is about 1.5e-4 m/s^2 per m/s, orbital tidal terms about 6e-5 m/s^2 at 15 m, DERIVED), or do they vanish in rounding and need accumulation in f64?

Is a bit-exact generator achievable across the phone, the browser and the build server when it needs square roots, logarithms and trigonometry in f64, or must it be written in integer or fixed-point arithmetic with its own math library?
How should the thermal budget be split when two regions are awake at once, and what is the smallest useful region (bodies and particles) that still feels alive?

Which ephemeris form is best on the phone: analytic Kepler elements, or a pre-integrated N-body table (size, accuracy over decades, evaluation cost), and do players need effects only N-body gives, such as Lagrange points?
What happens during atmospheric entry or a landing approach, when the region moves about 128 m per frame at orbital speed (DERIVED from 7.67 km/s at 60 Hz) and terrain must be generated ahead of it?

Can a second WebAssembly thread be used for background generation on the chosen host (cross-origin isolation was flagged as unavailable on GitHub Pages in the earlier research), or must generation be time-sliced on the physics thread?

The developer accounts for Outer Wilds, Star Citizen, KSP2, Noita, Universe Sandbox, Elite Dangerous and the Carlson-Hodgins and Chenney papers could not be opened in this session; their details (chunk sizes, zone mechanics, switching criteria, reported speedups) should be re-checked against the primary sources before any design decision leans on them.

redteam:physics.lens: Physics, first-principles integrity and completeness of 03-plan.md, on its own terms and as the innermost region of a solar-system-scale engine
redteam:physics.verdict: The synthesized plan does fix the solver-level fatal flaws of the candidates (pairwise velocity-level impulses plus reduced-coordinate articulations at one global 480 steps per second; softened FEM and the single energy-minimising solver removed; probe first; mechanisms first). But it is a summary that keeps the names of the honesty machinery while dropping about 55 concrete review fixes, and three fatal-class physics defects survive in weaker form: break/yield loads that the rigid tier does not determine, explicit softening of granular and soft matter, and an unspecified lagged CPU-GPU coupling. Its charter is also internally inconsistent (uniform gravity is unlisted hard-coded physics; 'one sanctioned departure' is at least three; the governor changes outcomes; switching was 'dropped' yet melting and breaking need it). Against the new requirement the decisive problem is that Layer 1, declared permanent, describes a closed, flat, airless, single-frame, constant-g, one-clock world: it has no reference frames, no field laws, no open ledgered boundary and no hand-off contract, so it cannot be embedded in a larger engine without changing the permanent layer. No code exists, so all of this is cheap to correct now; none of it requires abandoning the laws-and-materials-over-replaceable-solvers idea. All numbers below are tagged; I re-derived them in a scratch calculation and fetched Box2D defaults and three constants from source, but did not re-verify the research's device figures.

issues.issue: Layer 1, declared permanent, has no reference-frame concept: state is implicitly absolute position and velocity from one origin in one inertial frame, at a precision the plan never states. That cannot be embedded on a rotating planet, in orbit, or anywhere far from the origin, and every solver kernel will be written against it.
issues.evidence: DERIVED: the per-substep gravity increment is g*dt^2 = 9.81/480^2 = 42.6 um, while f32 spacing 2^(e-23) is 61 um from 512 m, 0.5 m at Earth's radius (MEASURED 6371 km, Wikipedia 'Earth radius') and 16.4 km at 1 AU (MEASURED 149,597,870,700 m, Wikipedia); even f64 at 1 AU is 2^(37-52) = 30.5 um, above the 17 um static contact sag the STRATA physics review derived. DERIVED: low-orbit speed sqrt(GM/r) = sqrt(3.986e14/6.771e6) = 7.67 km/s is 16 m per substep. MEASURED: the Box2D lineage rescales any body faster than 400 m/s by default (box2d src/types.c maximumLinearSpeed and src/solver.c, fetched 2026-11-24).
issues.fix: Make the frame a first-class Layer 1 object before Phase 0b: every simulated region owns a frame (f64 or fixed-point origin, velocity, angular velocity, parent) and all solver state is frame-local deltas, with integer tick time. Add translation, rotation and Galilean-boost invariance gates plus a far-from-origin resting test to the Phase 0b suite.

issues.issue: The plan models a closed world: it deleted representation switching, forbids creating matter or setting velocities, and describes everything outside the awake set only as 'sleeping or simplified matter'. The innermost region of a larger engine must continuously import and export bodies and matter across its boundary, which is exactly the creation, teleport and hand-off the plan has no conserving contract for.
issues.evidence: Plan lines 45-46, 72 and 110. The STRATA physics review's fix for 'bodies leaving the awake bubble have no stated representation, so their momentum can simply vanish' and for the particle-window flux boundary was not carried over. Without it the ladder's 'exact by construction: mass, momentum' holds only while nothing crosses the region edge.
issues.fix: Add to Layer 1 a boundary port with per-step flux accounts for mass, linear momentum, angular momentum and total energy, and a hand-off contract: aggregate mass, centre of mass, inertia tensor, momenta and energy must match across a representation change to a stated tolerance, with the residual booked. Reserve worst-case promotion cost at admission, and treat engine-internal hand-offs as an audited class separate from game escape hatches.

issues.issue: Charter rule 1 claims conservation laws are the only hard-coded physics, yet uniform constant gravity is a hard-coded force law the charter never names, and the ledger's potential energy is implicitly m*g*h in one frame. There is no place for a gravitational field, fictitious-force work, frame-transfer terms or radiative flux.
issues.evidence: DERIVED: g scales as (R/(R+h))^2, so -3.1% at 100 km and -11.5% at 400 km, and its direction tilts L/R = 1.6e-4 rad per km; Earth-surface Coriolis 2*7.292e-5*v is 1.5e-3 m/s^2 at 10 m/s, but in a 100 m radius habitat spun to 1 g (omega = sqrt(9.81/100) = 0.313 rad/s) it is 0.63 m/s^2 per m/s, 6.4% of g. DERIVED: Earth's orbital kinetic energy 0.5*5.97e24*29780^2 = 2.6e33 J (mass and speed from memory) has f64 spacing 2^59 = 5.8e17 J, so one global ledger cannot hold a planet and a robot.
issues.fix: Add a 'fields and interactions' class to the charter: Newtonian gravitation is the law, uniform g is its declared local approximation with the error reported per region. Define the ledger per frame with explicit gravitational-potential, fictitious-force, frame-transfer and radiative terms, and make ledgers hierarchical so each closes at its own magnitude.

issues.issue: Bend, yield and break are decided from joint and contact loads that the rigid tier does not determine physically, and quasi-static linear modal elasticity can neither vibrate nor buckle. Phase 2's gates (vibration frequency and buckling load within 3-5%, 'a bridge fails where the analysis says') cannot pass as designed for redundant structures, impacts or slender members; this is STRATA physics fatal flaw 2, inherited.
issues.evidence: DERIVED: at a 120 Hz contact clamp peak impact force is m*v*omega = 754 N per kg*m/s, while Hertz for a 1 kg steel sphere (R = 31 mm, E* = 110 GPa) at 1 m/s gives F = k*d^1.5 = 16.7 kN with k = (4/3)*E*sqrt(R) and d = (5*m*v^2/(4k))^0.4 = 75 um, a 22x gap. The STRATA physics review's numerical check (its DERIVED figures) gave tip-deflection errors of 23/13/7% for 4/8/16 free-free modes loaded through a weld, showed redundant load sharing follows soft-constraint compliance and sweep order, and that members with slenderness above 199 buckle below the 0.2-yield screen.
issues.fix: Solve each bonded or jointed assembly as an elastic network with real stiffness ratios (direct factorisation per island), bake Craig-Bampton attachment modes and geometric-stiffness buckling factors, and use impulse or energy criteria for impact damage. Make modes below the resolvable frequency dynamic state (DERIVED: a 1 m x 1 cm steel cantilever's first mode is 0.56*5048*0.00289/1^2 = 8.2 Hz), and gate with a redundant truss against the stiffness method through the runtime weld port.

issues.issue: Two-way coupling between the bit-exact CPU tier and the f32 GPU tier is one sentence with no scheme. A lagged partitioned exchange is where momentum stops being 'exact by construction' and where floating bodies go unstable, so Phase 3's boat gate either fails or is passed by an undeclared stabiliser.
issues.evidence: DERIVED: a hull with 5 cm draft heaves at T = 2*pi*sqrt(0.05/9.81) = 0.45 s (omega = 14 rad/s); a lag tau on the restoring force gives negative damping omega*tau/2 = 12% at one frame and 23-35% at the 2-3 frame readback delay two reviews assumed (ESTIMATE, unmeasured on iOS). Three reviews cite the added-mass instability of loosely coupled incompressible schemes when added mass exceeds body mass (from memory, unverified); a floating body displaces its own mass, so every boat sits near that limit.
issues.fix: Put rigid-body degrees of freedom inside the pressure projection (or integrate coupled bodies' free motion on the GPU), use a fixed N-tick delay line, and record the quantised wrench stream as a replay input. Gate with a bobbing float at density ratios 0.1-0.5, heave period and decay, and a 60 s at-rest drift test; measure readback latency in Phase 0a.

issues.issue: The 'one sanctioned departure' (rigid solids, incompressible liquids) does not cover sand, mud or soft solids, which the matter tier still promises. Explicit elasticity at 2-8 substeps forces their moduli down by orders of magnitude, the reviews' softening-admissibility rule was dropped rather than met, and materials between gel and rigid (rubber, foam) have no honest representation in either tier.
issues.evidence: DERIVED: c_max = dx*60*n at CFL 1, so at dx 2 cm and n = 2/4/8 the cap is 2.4/4.8/9.6 m/s, a modulus rho*c^2 of 5.8/23/92 kPa at 1000 kg/m^3. DERIVED: tyre rubber at 5 MPa and 1100 kg/m^3 (review's figures, ESTIMATE) has c = 67 m/s, 56 substeps per frame; 'a few litres of sand' (3 L, a 14.4 cm cube) strains g*h/c^2 = 6.1% at its base at 4 substeps and 2 cm cells, or 24.5% at 1 cm cells. Column collapse and angle of repose depend mainly on friction angle, so the Phase 4 gates would not detect it.
issues.fix: Treat the volumetric response of all dense matter with a unilateral implicit pressure projection and cap only the deviatoric modulus, or use an implicit or rigid-plastic granular solve. Add static-bed settlement and bearing-capacity gates at the shipped tier, restore the admissibility rule, and print 'unsupported' on the fidelity record for the gel-to-rigid gap until a representation exists.

issues.issue: Liquid, ground and (absent) air exist only as awake particles or rigid bodies inside a fixed window; there is no analytic or field far-field. So the boat floats in litres, the digger has litres of soil, and a planet's ocean, terrain and atmosphere have no representation the window could be embedded in.
issues.evidence: DERIVED: 10-30 thousand particles (plan estimate) at 8 per 2 cm cell is 1 mL each, i.e. 10-30 L. The Hamilton physics fix (Tier 1 analytic hydrostatic reservoir with the particle window embedded) and STRATA's kept idea (integrated-pressure buoyancy on analytic and heightfield liquids) are both absent from the plan.
issues.fix: Add field representations for bulk media to Layer 1 (hydrostatic or heightfield liquid, terrain as heightfield or SDF with a material, ambient gas), with Archimedes buoyancy integrated over the wetted hull as a convergent-tier result. Embed the particle window through a two-way flux boundary with mass and wave-reflection gates, and let the window move and re-orient with the local frame and gravity.

issues.issue: 'Contact stiffness and friction are derived from material data, then clamped' presents a clamp as a material law: above the clamp every solid has the same contact stiffness, so the derivation is vacuous. The Soft Step lineage also brings tuned constants and silent clamps the plan does not list among its declared approximations (charter rule 3), and 'the one sanctioned departure' is false by at least three (contact clamp, softened granular/soft matter, solver constants).
issues.evidence: DERIVED: at a 120 Hz clamp k = m*(2*pi*120)^2 = 5.7e5 N/m per kg for any material (STRATA physics review). MEASURED (box2d src/types.c and src/solver.c, fetched 2026-11-24): contactHertz 30, contactDampingRatio 10, contactSpeed (push-out) 3 m/s, restitutionThreshold 1 m/s, maximumLinearSpeed 400 m/s enforced by rescaling velocity, sleepThreshold 0.05 m/s, and a source comment that time-of-impact 'timeloss means there is a lost gravity contribution'.
issues.fix: State contact stiffness as a numerical regularisation, not a material property, and compute Hertz quantities (patch radius, peak-force estimates) analytically from the real moduli. List every solver constant, clamp and sleep rule in the Reality Report with a sensitivity test, and book any momentum or energy they remove.

issues.issue: The ledger's 'numerical loss' account is undefined; if it is the residual, closure is automatic and the audit proves nothing. In a soft-constraint solver most contact energy leaves through numerical damping, so the physical/numerical split is undefined exactly where most energy is dissipated.
issues.evidence: DERIVED: an implicit soft constraint keeps 1/(1+(h*omega)^2) of modal energy per substep, 29% at h*omega = pi/2. Two reviews (Hamilton physics, Materia physics) asked for independently computed channels and a cap; the plan kept only the phrase 'a separate numerical loss account'.
issues.fix: Compute every physical channel independently (friction work, restitution loss defined as (1-e^2) of normal relative kinetic energy, viscous and plastic dissipation, Joule heat) and define numerical loss as what remains. Gate numerical loss as a maximum fraction of physical dissipation on named scenes (ring-down, rebound height, slosh decay).

issues.issue: Stored elastic energy has no faithful home. In quasi-static modal elasticity strain energy is not a state variable (deflection is either cosmetic or moves geometry with no energy account), and springs integrated as implicit soft constraints lose energy at first order in the step, so bows, catapults, suspensions and springboards are wrong by tens of percent and depend on the step rate.
issues.evidence: DERIVED: energy kept over a quarter period is (1+(omega*h)^2)^(-pi/(2*omega*h)), about exp(-(pi/2)*omega*h), so at 480 steps per second a 5/10/20 Hz spring delivers about 90/81/66% of its stored energy. The Hamilton physics review's numeric check for a backward-Euler update gave 90/79/60%.
issues.fix: Integrate resolvable conservative elements (springs, modes below the clamp) with a second-order energy-consistent rule and carry their strain energy in the ledger as state. Add spring-launch efficiency tests at 5-50 Hz and a ring-down test with zero physical damping.

issues.issue: There is no tunnelling policy: no continuous collision detection, no stated speed envelope and no test.
issues.evidence: DERIVED: at 480 steps per second a body moves v/480 per substep, 10.4 cm at 50 m/s, so any dynamic pair thinner than that can pass through each other; at an orbital relative speed of 7.67 km/s it is 16 m. The research notes dynamic-versus-dynamic CCD is off by default in Box2D v3 and Box3D.
issues.fix: Always-on speculative plus time-of-impact CCD against statics, opt-in dynamic CCD, a declared envelope (minimum thickness times step rate) on the fidelity record, bullet and grazing tests, and frame-relative velocities so bulk orbital speed never reaches the contact solver. Declare hypervelocity impact out of scope.

issues.issue: The matter tier's boundary physics is unspecified: grid-based colliders cannot separate matter across walls thinner than about two cells, separate matter bodies fuse through the shared velocity field, and 'coupled with friction' is not a physical boundary condition for a viscous liquid. Viscosity itself is unresolved for thin liquids, which the plan does not declare.
issues.evidence: DERIVED: two cells at dx 2 cm is a 4 cm minimum wall, thicker than any cup, pipe or model hull (two-cell limit from the Materia physics review). DERIVED: the cell Reynolds number U*dx/nu = 1*0.02/1e-6 = 2e4 for water at 1 m/s, so molecular viscosity is far below grid-scale numerical dissipation and water and light oil behave identically.
issues.fix: Use a per-particle side-of-surface test (CPIC style) or particle-level SDF projection, per-owner two-field nodal contact, and no-slip or Navier-slip for liquids with Coulomb only for granular matter. Print minimum wall thickness and the viscosity floor on the fidelity record, and add a zero-leak thin-container test.

issues.issue: Phase 4 adds conduction and melting with no heat sink: no ambient reservoir, convection or radiation, and no temperature state for rigid bodies. Fire, combustion and a gas phase are neither scheduled nor listed as out of scope.
issues.evidence: DERIVED: 20 W of motor loss into a 0.5 kg steel housing (c = 490 J/kg/K, ESTIMATE from memory) heats it 20/(0.5*490) = 0.082 K/s, +98 K over a 20-minute session with nowhere to go. DERIVED: a 300 K black surface radiates sigma*T^4 = 5.67e-8*300^4 = 459 W/m^2, the only sink in vacuum; the Materia physics review derived that the Stefan gate can pass while in-game melting is grid-controlled (boundary layer sqrt(alpha*t) = 2.9 mm after 60 s against 2 cm cells).
issues.fix: Give each rigid body a lumped or coarse enthalpy, add an ambient reservoir with a declared film coefficient and grey-body radiation with measured emissivity, and book both in the ledger. State plainly whether fire is in or out.

issues.issue: There is no ambient medium: no drag, no buoyancy in air, no ambient pressure, no wind. This is an undeclared approximation (the out-of-scope list names turbulence, not air), it is visibly wrong at workshop scale, and at system scale the same vehicle must behave correctly in air, thin air and vacuum.
issues.evidence: DERIVED: drag 0.5*rho*v^2*Cd*A on a 6 cm ball at 20 m/s is 0.5*1.225*400*0.47*2.83e-3 = 0.33 N (Cd 0.47 for a sphere, ESTIMATE), 58% of the weight of a 57 g ball. DERIVED: sea-level pressure of 101 kPa (standard value) puts 10 kN on a 0.1 m^2 panel, which matters for any sealed or evacuated part.
issues.fix: Add an ambient-medium field to Layer 1 (density, pressure, temperature and velocity as functions of position, supplied by the outer tier; vacuum is a value, not the absence of the feature). Use a declared quasi-steady surface-element drag and lift closure in the empirical tier, air buoyancy, and ambient pressure as the matter tier's free-surface boundary condition.

issues.issue: The thermal governor contradicts its own rule: reducing awake matter freezes matter the laws say should move, so outcomes depend on device temperature. Governor actions are not listed as replay inputs, time dilation is never mentioned, the web has no thermal-state signal, and the default 'drop to 30 frames per second' makes the '60 Hz for 20 minutes' exits ambiguous.
issues.evidence: Plan lines 76-77 and 121-122 against the bit-exact replay claim at lines 87-89. Three reviews (Materia feasibility, Materia physics, STRATA physics) asked for refusal or shedding to be replaced by declared time dilation with worst-case certification at authoring time; one (Hamilton feasibility) asked for logged shedding, and the plan adopted the shedding without the logging.
issues.fix: Order the rungs: render scale, 30 Hz presentation with physics unchanged, declared time dilation, and only then logged matter reduction booked in the ledger. Record every governor decision in the replay stream, certify scenes on worst-case awake matter, and write exits as sim-time ratio plus dropped-frame fraction.

issues.issue: Rolling contact is unaddressed although the first mechanism milestone is a rover: no wheel or cylinder primitive, no per-substep contact refresh, no rolling-resistance property, no tyre model and no rolling test.
issues.evidence: DERIVED: with contact anchors fixed for a frame (confirmed in Box2D source by the STRATA physics review) a wheel unloads within the frame once v^2/r exceeds g, i.e. above sqrt(9.81*0.05) = 0.70 m/s for a 5 cm wheel and 1.7 m/s for a 0.3 m wheel, giving 60 Hz traction ripple. Hertz patch radius scales as E^(-1/3), so a patch computed from a clamped modulus is 27-126x too large (Hamilton physics review, DERIVED there).
issues.fix: Add analytic wheel and cylinder contact refreshed every substep, a declared rolling-resistance closure computed from real moduli, and for vehicles a brush-tyre or enclosed-gas tyre model. Gate Phase 1 with rolling acceleration ((5/7)*g*sin(theta) for a sphere) and traction at speed.

issues.issue: No gate is bound to the shipped configuration, so tests can pass on the f64 reference at fine resolution while the phone runs something never validated. Some stated tolerances are unreachable at the stated particle budget, and tests for the artifacts that break real mechanisms are absent.
issues.evidence: ESTIMATE: the free surface is located to about +/-0.5 cell; DERIVED from that: hydrostatic error is 0.5/N for an N-cell column, so 3% needs N >= 17, and a 17-cell cube at 8 particles per cell is 39 thousand particles, above the plan's 10-30 thousand. The STRATA physics review derived that a 5% waterline needs a hull 30-60 cells wide because grid contact acts 0.25-0.5 cell off the surface.
issues.fix: Run every gate on production precision at shipped dx, dt, particle count and iteration budget and publish those numbers beside the reference. Add step-rate invariance (240/480/960 per second), long-run liquid volume drift, resting jitter, four-bar closure drift, loaded transmission ratio, gyroscopic precession, spinning-assembly angular momentum and static-friction creep tests.

issues.issue: The plan says automatic rigid-to-deformable switching was dropped, yet melting (Phase 4), breaking (Phase 2) and digging all move matter between a rigid body and particles or create new bodies at runtime. None of that transfer is specified, so mass, momentum and energy at those events are unaccounted and runtime re-baking is unbudgeted.
issues.evidence: Plan lines 61-63, 100 and 110 contradict each other. The reviews' fixes (surface-layer promotion with remainder mass properties and reserved slots; pre-fractured or lattice fragments that stay plain rigid; fracture energy per crack area at two resolutions) are absent, and strain energy released at fracture is not a state in a quasi-static model.
issues.fix: Specify one audited conversion primitive (rigid volume to particles and back) that preserves mass, momentum, angular momentum and enthalpy, with reserved slots and the remainder's mass properties updated. Pre-bake fracture patterns offline, keep fragments plain rigid, and book fracture energy as toughness times crack area.

issues.issue: Activity management assumes gravity pins things to a ground frame and one clock runs everything at 480 steps per second forever. In free fall nothing comes to rest, coasting lasts hours to years, and 'never change the timestep' plus bit-exact replay leave no way to skip time.
issues.evidence: DERIVED: one year is 3.156e7 s x 480 = 1.5e10 steps; a signed 32-bit step counter overflows after 2^31/480 s = 51.8 days; f32 seconds cannot resolve one substep after 16,384 s (4.6 h), where spacing reaches 2^-9 s. MEASURED: the lineage's sleep test is a speed threshold, 0.05 m/s by default (box2d src/types.c), which presumes a rest frame.
issues.fix: Define a dormant representation: an assembly frozen into one aggregate rigid body (or point mass) on an analytic or coarse-step trajectory with its internal state stored, plus explicit wake conditions. Use an i64 tick clock with a declared multi-rate mapping, allow time acceleration only when every active region is dormant, and record rate changes in the replay stream.

issues.issue: The builder API is a list of nouns and becomes a usable kit only in Phase 6. Strict mode forbids spawning, teleporting and velocity setting, which a streamed large world needs constantly, and the plan does not say what language games are written in, at what rate controllers run, or how a game learns that something happened.
issues.evidence: Plan lines 70-74 and the Phase 6 row. Reviews asked for an event stream, a controller library with step-rate servo blocks, an authoring binding, implicit joint-housing collision exclusion, measured mass properties with provenance and an SDK slice from Phase 2; none appear.
issues.fix: Specify the API contract early: authoring binding, deterministic controller runtime and rate, events (contact, yield, break, sleep, hand-off), scene queries, snapshots and a stock controller library. Separate engine-internal streaming and hand-offs (audited, conserving) from game escape hatches, and end each phase with a small playable slice.

issues.issue: 'Motor tests within 1-2%' is unreachable for transients of small motors under first-order integration at 480 steps per second, and the electrical time constant is below one step.
issues.evidence: DERIVED: backward Euler turns a time constant tau into h/ln(1+h/tau), about tau + h/2, an error of h/(2*tau) = 5.2% at tau = 20 ms and 10% at 10 ms (typical small-motor mechanical time constants, ESTIMATE). ESTIMATE: small DC motors have L/R near 0.5 ms against a 2.08 ms step, so inductance must be dropped.
issues.fix: Integrate the linear motor-circuit-rotor subsystem with its exact exponential update, declare the zero-inductance approximation on the fidelity record, and name the motor tests (stall, no-load, step response, efficiency).

issues.issue: The determinism claims are broader than the design supports: a phone replay reproduces on the build server only for scenes that never touch GPU matter, the governor or timing-dependent input, and 'twice the bodies natively with identical hashes' conflicts with how the lineage obtains determinism.
issues.evidence: The research (lines 193 and 251, citing Rapier's documentation; not re-checked by me) says Rapier's enhanced-determinism feature cannot be combined with its SIMD feature. ESTIMATE (Hamilton feasibility review): two performance cores shared with rendering give about 1.3-1.6x, not 2x.

issues.issue: Several headline numbers are stated more firmly or more favourably than the research supports.

The research's own scaling gives 15-28 thousand particles cool and 10-17 thousand after derate for a lighter native kernel (low confidence), and reviewers corrected to 3-8 thousand liquid particles and 1-3 thousand honest sand (ESTIMATES) against the plan's 10-30 thousand; '4.3 W sustained' is one unverified excerpt of a 30-minute run on an A16 phone that is not the iPhone 15.
