small_world_assumptions: Constant, uniform gravity vector (never named in the plan; the lineage's world default is a fixed vector, MEASURED: box2d src/types.c). DERIVED with R = 6371 km (MEASURED, Wikipedia 'Earth radius'): magnitude scales as (R/(R+h))^2, so -0.31% at 10 km, -3.1% at 100 km, -11.5% at 400 km; direction tilts L/R = 1.6e-4 rad per km and a flat floor departs from the sphere by L^2/(2R) = 7.8 cm at 1 km and 7.8 m at 10 km.

One inertial frame with no fictitious forces. DERIVED: Earth-fixed Coriolis 2*Omega*v = 1.5e-3 m/s^2 at 10 m/s and equatorial centrifugal Omega^2*R = 0.034 m/s^2 (0.35% of g), with Omega = 7.292e-5 rad/s (from memory); in a 100 m radius habitat spun to 1 g, Coriolis is 6.4% of g per m/s. In orbit the natural frame is free-falling and only the tidal gradient 2GM/r^3 = 2.6e-6 s^-2 remains (DERIVED from GM = 3.986e14 m^3/s^2, MEASURED, Wikipedia 'Standard gravitational parameter', at r = 6771 km), which still separates two parts 10 m apart by 0.5*2.6e-5*100^2 = 0.13 m in 100 s.

Positions as offsets from one origin at an unstated (presumably single) precision. DERIVED: f32 spacing 2^(e-23) is 7.6 um at 100 m, 61 um from 512 m (already above the 42.6 um per-substep gravity increment 9.81/480^2), 1 mm at 10 km, 0.5 m at Earth's radius and 16.4 km at 1 AU; f64 from a heliocentric origin is 30.5 um at 1 AU and 1 mm at 30 AU, so even double precision needs local frames.

Absolute velocities inside the solver. DERIVED: low-orbit speed 7.67 km/s and Earth's heliocentric 29.8 km/s (from memory) are 16 m and 62 m per substep; f32 velocity spacing at 29.8 km/s is 2 mm/s against a per-substep gravity increment of 9.81/480 = 20 mm/s. MEASURED: the lineage's default speed clamp is 400 m/s (box2d src/types.c).

One clock at a fixed 480 steps per second with no time skipping. DERIVED: a year is 1.5e10 steps, a signed 32-bit step counter lasts 51.8 days and f32 seconds lose substep resolution after 4.6 h; the governor rule and the replay format both assume a single rate.

A fixed, world-axis-aligned window of matter with gravity along one grid axis, closed boundaries and zero ambient pressure; no moving or re-orienting window and no flux boundary to an ocean, soil or atmosphere reservoir. DERIVED: the window holds 10-30 L at 1 mL per particle (8 particles per 2 cm cell).

No atmosphere, and vacuum is not modelled as such either (no vapour pressure, no radiative cooling). DERIVED: sea-level drag on a 6 cm ball at 20 m/s is 0.33 N, 58% of a 57 g ball's weight (drag coefficient 0.47, ESTIMATE).

A ledger with only local terms: potential energy as m*g*h, kinetic energy in one frame, a single global sum, and no gravitational-field, orbital, frame-transfer, tidal or radiative terms. DERIVED: Earth's orbital kinetic energy of about 2.6e33 J has f64 spacing 2^59 = 5.8e17 J, so workshop-scale joules vanish in a global total. MEASURED: sunlight delivers 1.361 kW/m^2 at 1 AU (Wikipedia 'Solar constant') and nothing in the ledger can receive it.

Static ground of infinite mass as an unbooked momentum and energy sink. DERIVED: a 10 m diameter asteroid at 2500 kg/m^3 (density ESTIMATE) is (4/3)*pi*5^3*2500 = 1.3e6 kg with escape speed sqrt(2GM/r) = 5.9 mm/s; a 1 t lander arriving at 1 m/s changes its velocity by 1000/1.3e6 = 0.76 mm/s, 13% of escape speed.

Sleeping and the awake budget assume gravity presses things to rest against a ground frame; in free fall nothing settles, and a speed threshold (MEASURED: 0.05 m/s default, box2d src/types.c) has no meaning without a chosen frame.

Liquids assume gravity-dominated free surfaces and have no surface tension. DERIVED: the Bond number rho*g*L^2/sigma for 10 cm of water is 1000*9.81*0.01/0.072 = 1.4e3 at 1 g but 3.6e-3 under a 2.6e-5 m/s^2 tidal acceleration (sigma = 0.072 N/m, from memory), so in orbit capillarity governs and the tier's behaviour is qualitatively wrong.
Heat with no environment: no ambient temperature, no radiation and no solar input. DERIVED: in vacuum the only sink is radiation, 5.67e-8*300^4 = 459 W/m^2 from a 300 K black surface.

'Sleeping or simplified matter' as the only far-field: a planet's terrain, ocean and air cannot be sleeping rigid bodies or particles, and celestial bodies sit far outside the 1 cm to 10 m, 1 g to 10 t range the mechanism tier's parent design declared (STRATA's supported range).

Material data implicitly at room temperature and one atmosphere with no validity range; friction, restitution, modulus, lubrication and battery behaviour all change in vacuum and across the roughly 100-400 K range of space hardware (ESTIMATE).

The whole sustained power envelope (about 4.3 W, the plan's figure from an unverified excerpt) is spent on one awake workshop, with no share reserved for outer-tier work such as orbit propagation, frame management and streaming.

The player's finger is an actuator anchored to a ground-fixed view, and strict mode treats any spawn or velocity set as an escape hatch, both of which presume the camera and the world share one frame and that nothing streams in or out.

Gravity is implicitly Newtonian, instantaneous and single-source; n-body perturbations, light-time (DERIVED: 1.496e11 m / 2.998e8 m/s = 499 s at 1 AU) and relativistic effects are neither declared out of scope nor placed on the fidelity ladder.

Validation gates (hydrostatic pressure, dam break, angle of repose, waterline, pendulum) are all defined for uniform 1 g and a flat free surface, so none of them exercises the engine in a rotating, free-falling or low-gravity region.
keep: The laws-and-materials layer as the permanent asset with replaceable solver tiers beneath it (extend it with frames, fields and boundary ports; do not replace it)
Charter rules 3 to 5: every numerical shortcut declared and measured, every fidelity claim backed by an automated toleranced test, units enforced by types

The fidelity ladder's honesty: friction, restitution and viscosity labelled empirical; atoms, electromagnetic fields and turbulence out of scope; 'rigid plus incompressible' named as the stiff limit and reported per material
Per-step ledger of mass, momentum and energy with a separate numerical account, per-object fidelity record (authored versus achieved) and the live Reality Report

CPU mechanism tier built on pairwise velocity-level impulses with reduced-coordinate articulations at one global step rate; this is what resolves the candidates' angular-momentum and action-reaction fatal flaws
Solver choice settled by a written A/B test on the build server before anything is built on it
Physical actuator models: DC motor with back-EMF and current limit, gearbox reflected inertia, battery internal resistance; the finger as a force-limited actuator
Quasi-static modal elasticity at the real modulus as the stress estimator for stiff parts (extend it with attachment modes, geometric stiffness and plasticity; do not go back to softened FEM)
Implicit incompressible pressure solve for liquids; liquids are the one medium whose real stiffness limit is affordable on this phone
Strict mode by default with logged escape hatches whose injected mass, momentum and energy are booked as external
Bit-exact CPU tier with the WASM build as cross-platform reference, and a double-precision reference solver as oracle
Phase 0a probe on the actual phone before any budget is frozen; sustained power, not peak speed, as the binding budget; a 20-minute soak at the end of every phase; tests written before features
Mechanisms-first ordering and web-first delivery with native optional
The rejections recorded under 'What the reviews changed': no continuum-only engine, no single energy-minimising solver, no hand-off into a softened deformable solver
Presenting body and particle counts as unmeasured estimates to be replaced by the probe

redteam:feasibility.lens: Feasibility, delivery, scope and roadmap (adversarial review of /home/user/pulsevault/reality-engine/03-plan.md as a plan and as the future innermost region of a multi-scale engine)
redteam:feasibility.verdict: The workshop plan is a sound innermost region but not yet a deliverable plan: its headline scales are the pre-review research ranges (my re-derivation for the sustained web build is roughly 100-300 awake boxes and 3-8k liquid particles, ESTIMATE), most phase exits either cannot fail or cannot pass on the phone, and about two dozen feasibility fixes from the six reviews were silently dropped. With the solar-system requirement the roadmap order itself must change: the layer declared permanent has no frames, gravity model or time-scale policy, and no phase ever shows a second scale. The combined scope is finishable only with a hard v1 cut: probe, then a CPU-only two-scale release (f64 point-mass system tier plus one adopted-solver rigid workshop in a local frame whose gravity comes from the outer tier), then mechanisms; liquids become v2 behind a measured go/no-go, and sand, melting, yield/fracture, the native app and planetary surface detail are deferred. From this container WASM builds and WGSL on software Vulkan are workable (llvmpipe enumerates), but Safari's shader compiler and the deployed site are unreachable, so a macOS-runner Safari job, a post-deploy CI smoke test and on-page diagnostics are prerequisites.

issues.issue: No phase of the roadmap produces a second scale, and Layer 1 (declared permanent) has no reference frames, no gravity-source model and no time-scale policy. Phases 0b-6 would therefore build units, ledger, solver, replay and snapshot on single-origin, uniform-g, 1x-real-time assumptions that the new requirement invalidates.
issues.evidence: The only statement on scale in 03-plan.md is one sentence ('A larger world can exist around that as sleeping or simplified matter'); roadmap rows 0a-6 contain no frame, far-field or hand-off deliverable. DERIVED: an f64 heliocentric position at 1 AU (1.496e11 m, between 2^37 and 2^38) has ulp 2^-15 m = 30.5 micrometres, against a 480 Hz gravity step g*dt^2 = 9.81/480^2 = 42.6 micrometres, so the workshop cannot simply be dropped into a large f64 world.
issues.fix: Reorder: 0a probe, then a CPU-only two-scale release (f64 system tier of point-mass bodies plus one rigid workshop in a local frame whose gravity vector is supplied by the system tier), then mechanisms, then matter. Gate it with frame-invariance tests: identical workshop state hashes with the frame anchored at the origin and at 1 AU, and block fall time within 1% of sqrt(2h/g_local) on two different bodies.

issues.issue: The combined scope is not finishable as written: about 20 substantial subsystems (DERIVED by enumerating the plan's architecture and roadmap: units, materials, ledger, rigid solver, articulations, actuators, modal elasticity with yield and fracture, MPM with implicit pressure, two-way coupling, granular, plasticity, heat, renderer, governor, replay, native host, builder kit, game), each doubled by an f64 oracle, plus the new scale architecture. There are no durations, cut lines or kill criteria.
issues.evidence: The STRATA feasibility review judged a smaller version of this scope would 'stall after Phase 1 unless cut to about three representations', and every feasibility review asked for time boxes, which 03-plan.md omits. The only developer is a cloud agent in an ephemeral container and the only device is one phone operated by the user.
issues.fix: Define v1 as probe + two-scale rigid slice + mechanisms (joints, motors) + Reality Report + a toy built on the public API. Put liquids in v2 behind a measured go/no-go and remove from v1: Phase 4 (sand, mud, soft solids, melting), yield and fracture, the native app, more than one simultaneously awake detail region, atmospheres and terrain streaming. Give every phase a time box, a numeric floor and a named cut list.

issues.issue: The plan states scales but no frame or power budget, and its headline numbers are the research's pre-review ranges rather than the reviews' corrected ones.
issues.evidence: DERIVED from MEASURED Box3D M2 data in 01-research.md (5,050 boxes / 9.1 ms = 555 boxes/ms at 4 substeps; 555/1.7 = 326 at 8 substeps if the solver is 70% of cost, ESTIMATE) with ESTIMATE penalties (WASM 1.4-2.5x; immature or non-SIMD code 1-3.5x, bounded by the MEASURED Box2D float-versus-NEON ratio 4.64/1.36 = 3.4): 37-233 boxes/ms on one WASM thread, so 110-700 stacked boxes in 3 ms (central about 300) and about 35-210 convex hulls (hulls cost 3.3x, MEASURED). For liquids the reviews' corrected figure is 3-8k particles at 4 substeps (ESTIMATE; 3-8 L at 2 cm cells, DERIVED from 8 mL per cell at 8 particles per cell) and 1-3k for sand, against the plan's 10-30k.
issues.fix: Before the probe, publish a budget table derived from watts: about 5-6 ms of GPU in total and about 5 P-core-ms per frame sustained (the reviews' ESTIMATE from the 4.3 W anchor), split per tier, each line with a range and the probe measurement that will replace it. State web v1 targets as about 100-300 awake boxes (30-100 hulls) and 3-8k liquid particles until measured.

issues.issue: Phase 0a is not a days-sized milestone as written and its exit cannot fail. 'Real particle and rigid-body throughput' presupposes a solver and an MPM kernel chain, and 'every budget is replaced by a measurement' has no protocol, thresholds or decision table.
issues.evidence: All three feasibility reviews asked for a days-long probe with a written protocol, breadcrumb logs and a go/no-go ladder; the plan kept only the split into 0a and 0b. MEASURED this session: registry.npmjs.org returns 200 for @dimforge/rapier3d-compat (a prebuilt WASM rigid-body engine), so a real rigid benchmark needs no Rust build.
issues.fix: 0a-1 (ESTIMATE 1-2 days): plain JS page with adapter limits and features, timer resolution, memory growth, one compute dispatch, a 1,000-dispatch overhead batch, readback latency, a Worker WebGPU check, build hash and staged breadcrumbs. 0a-2 (ESTIMATE under a week): prebuilt Rapier box stacks at 100-2,000 bodies and 8 substeps, a minimal real MLS-MPM chain with sort and pressure sweeps at 4k/8k/16k particles, and a 20-minute soak at the planned duty cycle. Write the decision table first (which measured value selects which branch, e.g. under 4k sustained particles means the matter tier is deferred).

issues.issue: '60 Hz for 20 minutes' and 'the heat soak holds' are not falsifiable: no body or particle count and no metric. They also collide with the plan's own default (drop to 30 frames per second when hot) and with Safari halving requestAnimationFrame under thermal mitigation or Low Power Mode.
issues.evidence: MEASURED in 01-research.md from WebKit source: performance.now() resolution is 1 ms without cross-origin isolation, and requestAnimationFrame falls to 30 fps under thermal mitigation; the web has no thermal-state API. DERIVED: a hand-read battery percentage over a 20-minute soak at 4.3 W (4.3/3 = 1.43 Wh = 11% of the 12.98 Wh pack) has about +/-1 point of quantisation, i.e. about +/-9%, before battery-health scaling.
issues.fix: Define each exit as a stated scene size, simulation-time ratio 1.0 with zero dilation events, under 2% of frame intervals above 25 ms, and step time measured over batches of N ticks, under a written protocol (iOS build, tab or Home Screen, Low Power Mode off, unplugged, no case, fixed brightness, ambient, battery percent before and after). Declare 30 Hz presentation with two fixed steps per presented frame a certified pass state, and size sustained budgets at 0.5 of cool capacity.

issues.issue: The plan neither adopts a rigid-body library nor commits to writing one, and the 0b 'written A/B test' names no candidates, metrics or thresholds, so it cannot settle anything. A from-scratch deterministic 3D solver with reduced-coordinate articulations is far larger than one phase.
issues.evidence: Two reviews said to adopt Rapier. MEASURED this session from its Cargo.toml: version 0.36.1, Apache-2.0, minimum Rust 1.86 (the container has rustc 1.97), with rapier3d-f64 and rapier3d-mjcf crates and a 4-lane SIMD path; index.crates.io and static.crates.io return 200 while github.com clone URLs for third-party repositories return 403. Box3D is alpha v0.1 with six joint types and no articulations (MEASURED in 01-research.md).
issues.fix: Adopt Rapier, pinned and vendored from crates.io, behind the engine's own solver trait, and write only material-derived contact parameters with clamp reporting, actuators, ledger taps and frames. Turn the A/B into a pre-registered acceptance test of the adopted solver (cost per body-substep, 10-box stack drift, 1:1000 chain stretch, momentum defect, substep invariance) with a written fallback if it fails.

issues.issue: 'The whole loop runs from this Linux environment' is false in two places: nothing here can run WebKit's WGSL-to-Metal compiler, and the container cannot load the deployed site.
issues.evidence: MEASURED read-only in this container: rustc and cargo 1.97, Node 22.23, Chrome for Testing 153 (Playwright Chromium 1243), 4 vCPUs, 15 GB RAM, and a Vulkan loader 1.3.275 that enumerates 'llvmpipe (LLVM 20.1.2)' at API 1.4.335 when VK_ICD_FILENAMES=/opt/lavapipe/lvp_icd.json (no ICD is registered by default, there is no /dev/dri), plus a SwiftShader library. Missing: the wasm32-unknown-unknown target, wasm-bindgen-cli, wasm-opt, emscripten and any WebKit build; requests to rileykhalifaadam.github.io, webkit.org and the Playwright CDN got no HTTP response (curl code 000) and GitHub release downloads returned 403.
issues.fix: Gate every kernel through three compilers: naga via wgpu on lavapipe here, Tint via headless Chrome WebGPU here (not executed in this review because launching Chrome writes files, so verify it first), and Safari on a GitHub macOS runner (free for public repositories; whether the runner exposes WebGPU is unverified). Add a post-deploy smoke job in GitHub Actions, keep a CPU twin for every kernel, and treat an on-device subset as the real gate.

issues.issue: Phase 3's exit cannot pass on the phone as written: the particle tier is too small for the boat and hydrostatic gates, the coupling scheme is unspecified, and the implicit pressure solve is first costed inside Phase 3.
issues.evidence: DERIVED: a free-surface position error of 0.25-0.5 cell gives 3% hydrostatic error only below 8-17 cells of depth (0.25/0.03 to 0.5/0.03). The physics review's 5% waterline condition (hull 30-60 cells wide) means a half-submerged 30-cell hull displaces 30 x 30 x 15 = 13,500 cells = 108,000 particles at 8 per cell, against 3-8k (reviews) or 10-30k (plan). Reviews also showed that 16 Jacobi sweeps remove only about 37% of the smooth residual at 13 cells of depth (DERIVED there) and that lagged coupling is unstable when added mass exceeds body mass (ESTIMATE from memory in the review).
issues.fix: Restore the analytic or heightfield hydrostatic reservoir that two physics reviews recommended as the home for boats (it is also the mid-scale water representation a larger engine needs) and embed the particle window in it. Size each on-device gate to at most half the measured budget at shipped resolution, benchmark the pressure-solve chain in the probe, and put body inverse mass inside the pressure solve or use a fixed-delay over-estimated added mass with a bobbing-float gate.

issues.issue: On the web build the two tiers are not independent: encoding the GPU tier's compute dispatches, render submission and the mechanism solve share one thread, so 'one tier on the CPU, the other on the GPU' overstates what a combined scene can hold.
issues.evidence: Reviews counted 150-260 compute dispatches per frame for MPM with an implicit pressure solve at 4 substeps (DERIVED there by enumeration). At an ESTIMATE of 11-20 microseconds each that is 1.7-5.2 ms of CPU per frame (DERIVED), most of the roughly 5 P-core-ms sustained envelope (ESTIMATE), leaving 0-3 ms for mechanisms: about 0-300 boxes at the central 100 boxes/ms.
issues.fix: Budget dispatches as a first-class quantity (cap near 100 per frame, several block-local sweeps per dispatch) and measure per-dispatch cost and readback latency in the probe. Also test in the probe whether WebGPU works from a dedicated Worker (unverified), so the mechanism solve can leave the encoding thread without SharedArrayBuffer or nightly Rust.

issues.issue: The plan states no precision or coordinate policy. The design it was synthesized from used f32 positions about one origin limited to +/-128 m, and the GPU is fp32-only, which cannot serve as the innermost region of a moving frame.
issues.evidence: DERIVED: in an inertial frame at low-orbit speed 7.8 km/s (between 2^12 and 2^13) the f32 velocity ulp is 2^-11 = 4.9e-4 m/s, while one 480 Hz gravity increment is 9.81/480 = 0.0204 m/s, only 42 ulp. Two reviews already required island-local or f64-anchored positions 'from Phase 0' at workshop scale, and 03-plan.md dropped that.
issues.fix: Make co-moving local frames with f64 anchors and frame-relative f32 state part of Layer 1 in the first release, with frame acceleration and rotation as explicit ledgered terms. Add translation, Galilean-boost and rotating-frame invariance gates to the 0b suite.

issues.issue: Charter item 1 lists only the conservation laws and the second law as hard-coded physics, and the fixed-rate rule ('never changes the timestep') assumes 1x real time. A solar-system engine needs gravitation as a law and a time-acceleration policy, so the charter breaks the day the outer tier is added.
issues.evidence: 03-plan.md lines 17-18 and 76-77. DERIVED: an Earth-Mars transfer of about 259 days (ESTIMATE, the standard Hohmann figure from memory) compressed into 5 minutes needs 259 x 86,400 / 300 = about 74,600x time acceleration, while the workshop tier is already at its power limit at 1x.
issues.fix: Amend the charter now: add gravitation with a declared model per tier, make uniform g a derived local approximation with a reported error, and make time acceleration legal only for tiers whose integrators are certified at that step, with every detailed region asleep or on declared analytic rails.

issues.issue: The plan removed the intermediate representations its source design had (heightfield and analytic liquids, far-field ballistic bodies, an awake-bubble boundary), yet the middle scales, not the outermost one, are where a multi-scale engine's cost and content sit. No render budget exists anywhere in the plan.
issues.evidence: DERIVED: a 30-body gravitational system is 30 x 29 / 2 = 435 pair evaluations per step, microseconds per frame on one core (ESTIMATE of about 20 ns per pair), so the outer tier is nearly free. Planet terrain, oceans, atmosphere and their rendering must share the same roughly 5-6 ms sustained GPU envelope (ESTIMATE) as the matter tier, and the STRATA physics review warned that bodies leaving the awake bubble have no representation, so their momentum vanishes.
issues.fix: In v1 keep planets as gravity sources with one simple collision surface per landing site, give out-of-bubble bodies a ledgered ballistic or Kepler propagator, and state a render budget. Add heightfield terrain and reservoir water as the first mid-scale representations in v2, each with a ledgered hand-off.

issues.issue: Phase 2 rests on a method with no research backing and on gates the reviews' own checks contradict: 'quasi-static' modes have no vibration to measure, linear modes cannot buckle, and 'a bridge fails where the analysis says' names no structure, load or tolerance.
issues.evidence: MEASURED by search of 01-research.md: modal methods appear only in connection with sound. The STRATA physics reviewer's 200-element beam check (DERIVED there) gave tip deflection low by 23%, 13%, 7% and 3.6% with 4, 8, 16 and 32 free-free modes loaded through a weld, against the plan's 3-5% gate; re-baking modes for fragments on one WASM thread is unbudgeted.
issues.fix: Before Phase 2 is scheduled, pass a desktop prototype gate: Craig-Bampton attachment modes at joint anchors, exact oscillator integration for resolvable modes, baked linear-buckling factors and an elastic-network solve for bolted assemblies. Specify the bridge test as a named truss with member forces within a stated percentage of the stiffness method, and ship only elastic deflection and stress reporting first, with offline pre-fractured bakes later.

issues.issue: The determinism gates lack a transport and a compatible solver design. No path exists for a phone replay to reach the build server, GPU-coupled scenes need a recorded wrench stream, and Phase 5's 'identical replay hashes' between a one-thread WASM build and a two-thread NEON build requires a solver whose results do not depend on thread count or SIMD width.
issues.evidence: DERIVED: 20 minutes of 60 Hz touch samples is 72,000 x 16 B = 1.15 MB (about 1.5 MB as base64), and wrenches for 20 coupled bodies at 24 B and 60 Hz are 20 x 24 x 60 x 1,200 = 34.6 MB per 20 minutes; neither can be pasted. MEASURED: Rapier's determinism guide on master (possibly stale, it names features absent from the current Cargo.toml) says enhanced-determinism cannot be combined with SIMD or parallel features, which conflicts with the research note citing the changelog; only Box2D/Box3D claim invariance across thread counts by default.
issues.fix: Gate determinism on scripted-input scenarios that print a hash checkpoint every N seconds (a few hundred bytes to paste), with the build server running the same .wasm under Node, which is bit-exact by the WASM specification apart from NaN payloads. Keep full replay export as a file for bug reports, restate bit-exactness as holding for matter-free scenes or with recorded wrenches, and keep Phase 5's hash-equality gate only if the chosen solver is ordering-invariant by design.

issues.issue: A new public repository does not 'keep PulseVault untouched': a project site under the same account shares the origin rileykhalifaadam.github.io, so localStorage, OPFS and IndexedDB quota, the persistence grant and any 'clear website data' step are shared with the existing app. The subfolder alternative is worse, and GitHub Pages cannot send the cross-origin-isolation headers that threads and fine timers need.
issues.evidence: MEASURED in this repository: /home/user/pulsevault/README.md gives the live URL on that origin and says all PulseVault state lives in localStorage; /home/user/pulsevault/sw.js is network-first and caches every GET inside its /pulsevault/ scope, so a subfolder deploy would be intercepted, and .github/workflows/pages.yml copies a fixed file list that excludes reality-engine/. MEASURED from GitHub's docs source: published Pages sites are limited to 1 GB with a soft 100 GB per month bandwidth limit; Safari's localStorage quota of about 5 MB per origin is an ESTIMATE from memory.
issues.fix: Use a new repository, keep engine data in IndexedDB or OPFS under an engine-named database and directory, never write engine logs to localStorage, never instruct origin-wide clearing, and give any engine service worker its own path scope. Start single-threaded without isolation and add the coi-serviceworker shim only when threads or 20-microsecond timers are needed; a clean origin with real headers needs a different static host and a user account.

issues.issue: Buildability is proven last (Phase 6), and the plan never states what a game is written in (a Rust crate, or JavaScript/TypeScript over WASM) or ships a controller library. 'Driven only by voltages' makes each milestone demo a bespoke controls project, and API mistakes surface after six phases.
issues.evidence: Reviews asked for a usable SDK from Phase 2, a controller library and a playable toy at the end of every phase; 03-plan.md keeps the builder kit and first game as the final roadmap row. With the scale requirement the API must also expose frames, sites and time acceleration, none of which appear in the strict-mode description.
issues.fix: State the authoring binding now and end every release with a small toy built only on the public strict-mode API (first: throw blocks on two worlds and in orbit). Ship joint-servo, wheel-speed and inverse-kinematics controllers as ordinary strict-mode library code in the mechanisms phase.

issues.issue: The plan does not choose between wgpu and a hand-written WebGPU layer for Safari, and the inherited default (wgpu on the web) is the untested path.
issues.evidence: MEASURED in 01-research.md: wgpu's README and CI do not cover Safari, Bevy 0.20's wgpu shaders failed in Safari 26.6, and WebKit's WGSL compiler rejects constructs that naga and Tint accept (constant arrays above 2,047 elements, textures bound to let).
issues.fix: On the web use a thin hand-written JavaScript WebGPU host that binds WASM memory and loads plain .wgsl files; use wgpu natively for lavapipe tests here and for the later iOS host, both driven by one shared kernel manifest (bind layouts, buffer sizes). Prove one compute pass through the web path on the phone in 0a-1.

issues.issue: 'A double-precision reference solver ... for every production solver' roughly doubles the implementation work of each tier.
issues.evidence: The STRATA feasibility review flagged this as a scope multiplier. MEASURED this session: a rapier3d-f64 crate exists in Rapier's workspace and pypi.org's index page for mujoco returns 200 (download not attempted).
issues.fix: Write solvers generic over the float type and use the f64 instantiation with converged iterations as the reference. Use independent engines (Rapier f64, MuJoCo) offline in the container as cross-checks, and run every gate at shipped f32 resolution as well.

issues.issue: The governor's 'reduce the amount of awake matter' makes physical outcomes depend on phone temperature and is not listed as a replay input, which conflicts with 'never changes the laws' and with bit-exact replay.
issues.evidence: All three physics reviews flagged refusing or shedding awake matter as outcome-changing (a refused pile becomes an immovable momentum sink) and required governor decisions to be recorded as replay inputs. 03-plan.md lines 76-77 keep the shedding and say nothing about recording it.
issues.fix: Admit scenes against a worst-case awake budget at load time, record every governor decision in the replay stream, and order the rungs as render scale, 30 Hz presentation, then declared time dilation. Shed simulated matter only as a logged, ledgered demotion that uses the same rules as a scale hand-off.

issues.issue: The plan states 'an A16 phone sustains about 4.3 W' as fact, but it is a single unverified search excerpt, apparently about a different and larger phone, at unstated brightness.
issues.evidence: 01-research.md cites an article whose URL names the iPhone 15 Pro Max and marks it unverified; that host gave no HTTP response from this container. MEASURED on Wikipedia this session: the base iPhone 15 panel reaches 1,000 nits typical and 2,000 nits peak outdoors, far above the 150 nits at which the research's 0.94 W idle figure was taken.
issues.fix: Label 4.3 W an ESTIMATE, expect a lower envelope for the smaller chassis and for bright screens, fix brightness in the soak protocol, and let the probe's battery-percent measurement set the real figure.

issues.issue: The jump from 'hundreds' of bodies on the web to 'low thousands' natively, and Phase 5's 'at least twice the awake bodies' gate, contradict the plan's own statement that heat, not speed, is binding. Phase 5 also hides manual Apple steps.
issues.evidence: DERIVED from ESTIMATE factors: a second P-core gives 1.3-1.6x and removing WASM 1.4-2.5x, so 1.8-4x on a cool phone, but at a fixed power envelope only the efficiency part (1.4-2.5x) survives a 20-minute soak. Reviews found that fastlane cannot create the app record with an API key and that each native fix costs a 10-15 minute runner cycle (ESTIMATE in the review).
issues.fix: State the native target as body-steps per joule over a soak, about 1.5-2.5x the web build (ESTIMATE), and schedule an empty TestFlight build with a user preflight checklist before any porting. Keep Phase 5 deferred until the web ceiling is the measured blocker.

issues.issue: A CPU-only milestone can be blocked by a browser GPU bug, because the first playable scene has no renderer fallback and the plan no longer mentions snapshot and resume.
issues.evidence: 01-research.md lists WebKit bug 302711, a Metal-backend crash on iOS 26.0/26.1 that builds over about 70 seconds and scales with mesh count (unverified excerpt), and notes that iOS kills the tab instead of signalling device loss.
issues.fix: Draw all bodies in one instanced call, provide a WebGL2 or Canvas fallback for CPU-tier scenes, and make physics exits independent of the renderer. Persist snapshots and breadcrumbs so a tab kill is recoverable and diagnosable.

issues.issue: Toolchain set-up is not a deliverable, although the container is ephemeral and several download routes are blocked.
issues.evidence: MEASURED: no wasm32 target, no ~/.cargo/registry cache, no wasm-bindgen-cli or wasm-opt; static.rust-lang.org, index.crates.io, static.crates.io and registry.npmjs.org return 200, while github.com release and clone URLs return 403 (so the npm wasm-pack installer and cargo git dependencies will fail). The cold-start cost per session is an ESTIMATE of 10-20 minutes of installs and first builds on 4 vCPUs.
issues.fix: Make the first deliverable a pinned tool list and an in-repository bootstrap script (rustup target add, cargo-built wasm-bindgen-cli, binaryen from npm, Node as the WASM test runner), with a committed lockfile and crates.io-only dependencies. Do release builds in GitHub Actions with caching.

issues.issue: The plan lists five decisions but not the user's hands-on steps, and one stated constraint is unverified.
issues.evidence: Reviews found that a new repository's Pages source cannot be enabled with the workflow's own token. MEASURED: this checkout's only git remote is RileyKhalifaAdam/pulsevault, and this session's tool catalogue lists a GitHub repository-creation tool and an add-repository tool, so 'this session cannot create repositories' should be tested, not assumed (authorisation was not tested here).
issues.fix: Give one checklist: create or approve the public repository and choose a licence, set the Pages source to GitHub Actions, attach the repository to the session, confirm iOS 26 or later, then per phase run the written soak protocol and return results through a prefilled GitHub issue link instead of pasting. For Phase 5 add enrolment, agreements, app record, bundle ID and a Team API key placed directly in repository secrets.

issues.issue: Phase 4's gates have no tolerances ('match experiment') and bundle four research-grade features (granular flow, plasticity, conduction, melting) whose honest budget on the phone is tiny.
issues.evidence: Reviews derived that explicit sand holding self-weight strain near 1% needs 13-27 substeps at 2 cm cells, leaving about 1-3k particles (ESTIMATE; 1-3 L, DERIVED at 8 particles per 8 mL cell). The Materia physics review derived a thermal boundary layer of sqrt(1.43e-7 x 60) = 2.9 mm after 60 s against 2 cm cells, so the melting test can pass while in-game melting is grid-limited.
issues.fix: Remove Phase 4 from v1. When it is scheduled, give each feature its own gate with a numeric tolerance at shipped resolution, and treat dense granular volume with the same pressure projection as liquids.

dropped_review_fixes: Budget from watts instead of from a throttled frame: about 5-6 ms GPU total and about 5 P-core-ms per frame at the 4.3 W anchor, sustained budgets at 0.5 of cool capacity (reviewers' ESTIMATEs); 03-plan.md has no millisecond or watt table at all. [Hamilton, Materia, STRATA feasibility]

Corrected planning numbers: 3-8k liquid particles at 4 substeps, 1-3k for honest sand, 110-330 web boxes in 3 ms, 64-128 certified awake primitives for web v1 (all reviewers' ESTIMATEs); the plan reverted to the research's 10-30k particles and 'hundreds' of bodies. [STRATA, Materia feasibility]

Written soak protocol and falsifiable exits: simulation-time ratio 1.0, dropped-interval fraction, Low Power Mode off, stated brightness, no case, unplugged, ambient noted, battery percent as the power proxy. [all three feasibility reviews]
Numeric floors, time boxes, named cut lists and kill criteria per phase, with tolerances frozen in the phase that ships each feature. [all three feasibility reviews]

Diagnostics for a lab with no remote inspector: staged breadcrumb log, getCompilationInfo, uncapturederror and device.lost capture, build hash in the HUD and every report, cache-busted assets, one-tap result return instead of copy-paste. [Hamilton, Materia, STRATA feasibility]

Safari shader-compile job on a GitHub macOS runner and WGSL execution in the container as Phase 0 exit items; NaN-safe kernels because Safari compiles in relaxed-maths mode; a CPU twin for every kernel. [all three feasibility reviews]
Thin hand-written WebGPU host on the web, or proof of wgpu on the phone in the probe, before committing to wgpu for Safari. [Materia feasibility]

Adopt an existing deterministic rigid-body engine (Rapier) and write only the material, actuator and coupling layers; use Rapier, Box3D and MuJoCo as offline oracles. [Materia feasibility and physics, STRATA feasibility]
Solver A/B with thresholds fixed in advance: cost per body-substep, stack drift, chain stretch, momentum defect. [Hamilton feasibility and physics]

'Sleeping' means at rest in the world frame; on a rotating planet or in orbit a sleeping body is moving and needs rails propagation with ledger entries.

One global ledger of mass, momentum and energy: DERIVED, Earth's orbital kinetic energy 0.5 x 5.97e24 kg x (2.978e4 m/s)^2 = 2.6e33 J has an f64 ulp of 2^59 = 5.8e17 J, so workshop-scale joules vanish in a shared account; the source design's integer-microgram mass ledger overflows 64 bits for any planet (5.97e33 micrograms versus 2^64 = 1.8e19).
Snapshot equals the whole world and replay equals initial snapshot plus inputs from time zero; both assume the world fits in memory and sessions last about 20 minutes.
